Friends, This Memorial Day, we honor the Americans who gave their lives in service to this country and the ideals it represents. Their sacrifice reminds us that freedom, democracy, and fundamental rights are never guaranteed. They must be protected by every generation. At a time when voting rights and democratic freedoms are under growing strain across the country, Memorial Day takes on even deeper meaning. Because when some Americans face barriers to having their voices heard, when fundamental rights are weakened for some communities, none of us are truly free. The promise of this country belongs to all of us equally. And honoring those who served means continuing the work of protecting that promise. Today, we remember those we lost, reflect on the responsibilities we share, and recommit ourselves to the enduring ideals they fought to defend. Wishing you and your loved ones a meaningful and peaceful Memorial Day. —Voting Rights Fund
* * *
******
****** | Voting Rights Fund wasn’t created just to defend voting rights — we elect the leaders who will expand and protect them. Our aim is to keep our operational costs as low as possible, so a majority of our funds go toward doing the work that needs to be done. That means building a national bench of lawmakers who will fight tooth and nail to expand access to the ballot box and protect our right to vote at every level of government. **Learn more about how to join our pro-democracy movement »**

name: Matt Ortega
subject: A nation worthy of their sacrifice
body:
Honor them with a nation worthy of their sacrifice. | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.A3cd-kVlFz1CzUMSYeTvVdaU3GDudfHJ-LpMUWeRi9iuVBaY-E6iK8WBYDhBhwkgz6xblv2zBch8_eD9ilKXSQeszP4nb6RXEG7eEtNX9zmE9P0nZwqmu1otB1h109TDYEOIXXy96WE0ofbuuYSzaurwfssAqoMJbD6dx8FXVkRGaVGDSBHTfTs7pjXkHPC_a0ekShRz788ze2hoJUgA1MUyeQca-_yp53tOROHO0eEsvBHgHdplV9dypmp688yP/4qy/fHYoo7-iSO6ZmKDNFOhv3Q/h0/h001.ZaDx_7O1QG-_3mzaDuWDNP1KOOeLz1cTHkeIrHdpSiU) | Friend, Your inbox is undoubtedly filled with sales for various retailers right now. I wanted to take a momentary break from the discount codes and speak to you on this somber day of reflection. The communities which comprise the 14th Congressional District, in part or in whole, lost 12 of our neighbors in the conflicts since 9/11. The youngest, a Marine from Fremont, was just 19. He died in Iraq and would be 41 right now. I grew up with a particular reverence for the military. My grandmother would supply me with an endless supply of old TIME Life magazines from the war and various anniversaries that followed. My father was nominated to West Point by then-Rep. Ron Dellums in 1974 and later served with the 7th Army in Germany. My uncle John served in the 173rd in Vietnam. His booming calls of "Airborne!" still echo. My birthday happens to be November 11—Veterans' Day. On my 16th birthday, my uncle brought me to a parade to march with him and his friends. Afterward, sitting around a table for lunch, I was riveted with the stories they told. Men who served in combat. Occasionally, they would speak of someone and chuckles petered out into an extended silence. Every Memorial Day, I think about that table twenty-six years ago. I didn't know those they spoke of but in their faces I saw the impact on these tough men. Men I looked up to—and it made the loss more real than any magazine article or book could. **We owe a debt to those who didn't come home—and to their families—that we can never fully repay. But let us try and honor them with a nation worthy of their sacrifice.** A nation that treats war with the gravity it deserves. A nation that understands that the reasons we go to war always matter. And a nation that bears the full responsibility to care for the families of the fallen. We aren't there yet. If you lost a loved one who served, thank you for their service. May their memory be a blessing which carries with you. And may we, one day, be worthy of their sacrifice. Thank you. Matt

I've seen Big Government try to take away our rights with unconstitutional mandates and strip us of our individual liberties. Consider this my promise to you Peter - As your next Congressman, I will NEVER waver in my defense of you or our God-given liberties. Peter,
Poppy managed to score 3 bagels off the counter today while I was baking. While she’s in her carb coma, I’ve got a quick note for you.
We’re less than two weeks out from the June primary, ballots are in mailboxes, and _my opponents are spending millions trying to drown us out on the airwaves._
I’m up against a billionaire, a Big Oil-backed candidate, and MAGA Republicans who think if they spend enough money, they can buy their way onto November’s ballot.
I got into this race because Californians are getting _crushed_ by costs. Housing is too expensive. Health care is too expensive. Child care is too expensive. College is too expensive.
**I’m running to actually lower costs for working people.**
And here’s what’s at stake: _there’s a chance TWO MAGA Republicans advance to November with no Democrat on the general election ballot._
I don’t take corporate PAC money, and I’m not bankrolling my own campaign. I’m powered by people giving what they can because they want a governor who will fight for them—not for Big Oil, not for corporate lobbyists, and not for billionaires.

| | Dear Peter,
Our independent socialist campaign to elect Kshama Sawant to U.S. congress has now raised over $60,000 in the month of May! This has been done with a median donation of just $25, compared to Adam Smith’s median donation of $1,000, because Smith is funded by the super rich, the weapon’s industry, and Big Tech corporations going for broke on AI.
We now have just a week remaining to raise that $15,000 needed to hit our goal of $75,000 in May. Reaching $75K in May will get us to $600K overall. Smith will have millions of dollars behind him in this race, and has already raised over $1.2 million. The last thing the billionaires and their two parties want is Kshama Sawant in Congress, and Super PAC money will be backing Smith to the hilt.
We need to hit our goals in these final weeks in order to have a real shot to defeat warmonger Adam Smith. It costs over $100,000 to send out just one mailer in the 9th Congressional District, and Smith will send many such mailers. Donating will also help us to order more yard signs, posters, and campaign brochures, and to rent venues for our mass meetings as the election heats up, and build the strongest canvassing campaign the 9th Congressional District has seen in decades!
We could hit our goal with another 600 people donating $25, or 300 donating $50, or even 15 people donating $1,000. Whatever your financial situation, this independent socialist campaign needs your support. Donate today to help us hit this ambitious target and elect Kshama Sawant to Congress!
Kshama Sawant has been the strongest fighter for the working class in decades. She led the way to the first $15 minimum wage in a major city (now $21.30), a victory that alone has led to billions of dollars being transferred from the wealthiest corporations to the lowest-paid workers. She won over a billion dollars total in funding for affordable housing since the Amazon Tax first went into effect, free abortion in Seattle, and landmark renters rights laws that still have the corporate landlords in an uproar.
The billionaires' and multi-millionaires' response to growing economic turmoil is clear. They’re betting heavily on AI and a massive expansion of hyper-scale data centers to keep up their mega profits, and on more big corporate handouts from Democratic and Republican politicians to help them do that. The costs of this mass expansion of data centers on working people will include heavy pollution of drinking water, air pollution, noise pollution, and the driving up of utility costs. Meanwhile, tech companies are trying to use AI to carry out mass layoffs of workers far beyond the tens of thousands who’ve already lost their jobs.
Oracle laid off 18% of their workforce all at once on March 31st via a five line email at 6am. Oracle’s big shareholders were pleased by this attack, and they saw a 95% jump in profits that quarter. While this is the single largest recent mass layoff at tech companies, over 100,000 tech workers have been laid off in 2026 alone, and industry analysts have estimated that the number of tech workers laid off since generative AI tools were first introduced is over 500,000.
Kshama Sawant is the only candidate in this race fighting to stop the data centers and AI layoffs and to take these reckless Big Tech corporations into democratic public ownership. If Big Tech CEOs are allowed to, they will continue to drive both living standards and the climate over the cliff. But working people are fighting back, and a number of data centers have been blocked or put on hold.
We need to use this campaign to build a mass fight against the data centers and AI layoffs and send a proven working class fighter, Kshama Sawant, to Congress to stand up to Big Tech, the billionaires, and both their parties.
Donate now, and RSVP for our June 7th Town Hall about how we can fight back against the data centers and Big Tech.
In Solidarity,Justin BareCampaign ManagerKshama for Congress

All of the talking heads are talking about the House and Senate elections, and yes, those will be consequential. But here's the truth most political pundits and election analysts are missing:
The fate of Democracy will also hinge on often overlooked and underappreciated state Supreme Courts races.

The constitutionality of their actions will ultimately be decided by state Supreme Courts. That means whoever controls these courts will control the fate of our Democracy:

## Trump Pushes Muslim Nations to Join Iran Deal
President Trump on Monday declared it "mandatory" that Muslim nations [sign the Abraham Accords](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAQBuCnMZ0je8AGChfX0OXaK9EEj2FOxkbGSZS3X7H7CFuO5tf_S9-_-3xHjpzWv7iTqyHPid5npFqpzFwwecJ45INO5DeWxGnF5GdQYKUyEuzskeNn7hrvAhFQ25DTfT_2o9KdajbXhUfwShsYfYfWBlhCP-rQdsZbGlrdsLvalAGrlRrMcBtUP2ijjVW9JRy16BR5rrnc_mdOdaMQP_lF5bbkvYluq_U4RftHwCRgqhttHOP1EzAdOfLyETBxqlQSVs4Jo4DJDGM7jCD9dXtZy3M_5PqMQf6ETomPghvuEpclF3_K5ykvD3mBCJia4vzx5hj5tL3o1Lojf6829VeMLwdfAQAA__9GIYcx) as part of any Iran peace deal, calling out Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey, and Jordan by name. Trump pressed Saudi Arabia and Qatar to sign first, warning that holdouts would be cut from the deal entirely. Saudi Arabia had previously signaled openness, but only if there was a clear path toward a Palestinian state. Iran's top negotiator [arrived in Qatar](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOpBZsMGFizR0lzYl2sMLbGRsZDtn3d9H5BfSPWmk0cz7eiwPZMd-_8STTN7C4qkkRzlTXDiit4TuChcl5ILRs9_R2wUEqEbIBtRikd17GWprNiKgvibTjaMetegGUR9G62GVW28VkpK9tQga-w2eWiHCKnXN5m4TElQnxCSndhLj1MlOKjEqQt1VgyDLOcT2O7DPB23uHV4U2zWctTNHzleq-o8K5grmUkr7xiOEO61gvu9UMF_Bceb1RoyZV0c35vhzXo2lE71NTWFL6YqEtkm8-wafEQ88m24AKQfoZXvk09XR2Kuwc5zUWA1iP5Hd35T8L38vA78BAAD__xKehOE) Monday as talks continued, with Trump warning the outcome would be "a Great Deal for all or no Deal at all." The emerging framework is drawing pushback from some Republicans, with Sens. Roger Wicker and Lindsey Graham arguing that extending the ceasefire hands Iran an advantage.
## Pope Releases Encyclical Warning of AI Dangers
Pope Leo XIV released his first major encyclical Monday, [_Magnifica Humanitas_ ("Magnificent Humanity")](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU8DmVHZYBsCB5uQ9aYboqJdNLUyNsKmUd9-xGhuMEmppC89_ff_PaYHcuD4-osbubKkKdKVA5VCx8QHRk8Y9rRTRr7wiBxfGP2kQBkBWigzeeTwmbrau4VIUVuTk9YOdgDZQb06O3dWG9XC4HvZLWT0LKFDs8xtr9uWanY3DbQyEqDXfdOD7aWW2oA1hIOsOiDPJR3N_8SxrLSET3rT0TzTVge3lrLnqv1TqbFS43VdzTPOzzus1HijKzWCvv_73C4iUBKc80lZ_EhlgXM6i0AWGL3As6SYtnRmcRHuKeZmLVuoD-f3i0PgbGzVwWtDDt81yq-2ezv1FQAA__8ItIHj), calling on world governments to slow and tightly regulate artificial intelligence before it drives humanity toward what he called an era of unending war. The document warns that some autonomous weapons systems have advanced "practically beyond any human reach to govern them," and that [AI spreads misinformation,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ_GdCCzgA2FizR0lzYl2rPX3EZ7NjLWoXv7iLzC34000oy-789jeyALp_03vsnVmLdE1ylUK5WNC6ZAKEc-6ES-sCROO6awgQbT6qkFswVk-W5jE1wkAhoacr21i110P-rm5cbBaBPmYZj6EQFChDAMiw4x2Pn59LFhd6_pCUyv9TzN3azt3E_9ZLQ1hEuvRk2Bay7d38ypvijKN3-odD6_G3GvWo9TDb8UrArW67o6_zxvirtXsN5RwXpDtEK5RW4p-a8X9igtlsqRPaO0nCqJ8E7Jk4K1KS4cF4vwaawa9f5Glv-f9UeiPg7-BQAA__9hr31i) exploits workers, and threatens human dignity at a scale comparable to the Industrial Revolution. The encyclical also includes [a historic apology](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DEOnTAQBNDTmM5fa4MxFC7SIKX4aVKkRBuzwCbGRrb1CbePyBVSjzSaNz_e8xs5cNy-4UGurmmOdJVAtVKeOWNcCMOZTirIF-bIccO4zBp0L8FI3c8LcrjnrlncSqSpbcgpa0c7guqg2d1qtTdkvF89jBrs0q2gjAeAwWJLQ8PuaQOjewUwmOE1gB2UUaYH2xOOSnRAC9eUX78Sx7rTGu70ofzy6WiC22s9i2i_CD0JPeFP_wieTOjpa6yUI1ZOEYPQ08WZvteUb6GnRyUDJfmHP_LA31TkzqWmzF7imULabrmncMtCVKRqW23HUZsmu-W8OAQuvRUdbAdy-Del_td_H6f_BgAA___Z34TU) for the Holy See's own role in legitimizing slavery through 15th-century papal edicts, the first time any pope has acknowledged the Vatican's direct complicity, not merely Christians' participation.
## List: World's Tallest Buildings since 1909
A new timeline of skyscrapers [tracks the world's tallest building](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQAL8GOpDtAwOFizR0lzYlWuwFNloMsvfOur-PLr_w-tGMNH-eyxOIKe6_4UQn27VELJlRBNNCCWJA4Pu6MQMVSJHiDjEsRhnbqL4xdglA_Fm6OrgN0eCjRqeHYRompTtVHw79tmpvt81P1vt1tR6m3oRNrcM0BqNrcl-b6o3VSo392I5qGHWve6sGizDpqlMYSK7U_r0oyoEbf643ptZfZ83uELlz9fhVmbkycymlfVN-AXu4SYApyxeszCx0IlPERg5sypU45EaAGbM064s4UNxzZeY6uXAXYqZsh6pT-wnE_2Pyo0NvZ_4FAAD__7XOfN8) across more than a century, revealing America's longtime dominance before a striking geographic shift toward Asia. New York held the crown essentially continuously from 1909 to 1973, running up a string of record-holders, from the Met Life Tower to the Empire State Building to the World Trade Center North Tower. Then the title moved in 1974 to the former Sears Tower in Chicago (now the Willis Tower). Since 1998, the world's tallest building has been located in Asia. Malaysia's Petronas Towers kicked things off, followed by Taiwan's Taipei 101, and now Dubai's Burj Khalifa. The world's tallest building has grown from a height of 700 feet in 1909 to 2,717 feet today--nearly four times taller in just over a century. Pope Releases Encyclical Warning of AI Dangers Pope Leo XIV released his first major encyclical Monday, , calling on world governments to slow and tightly regulate artificial intelligence before it drives humanity toward what he called an era of unending war. The document warns that some autonomous weapons systems have advanced "practically beyond any human reach to govern them," and that exploits workers, and threatens human dignity at a scale comparable to the Industrial Revolution. The encyclical also includes for the Holy See's own role in legitimizing slavery through 15th-century papal edicts, the first time any pope has acknowledged the Vatican's direct complicity, not merely Christians' participation. List: World's Tallest Buildings since 1909 A new timeline of skyscrapers across more than a century, revealing America's longtime dominance before a striking geographic shift toward Asia. New York held the crown essentially continuously from 1909 to 1973, running up a string of record-holders, from the Met Life Tower to the Empire State Building to the World Trade Center North Tower. Then the title moved in 1974 to the former Sears Tower in Chicago (now the Willis Tower). Since 1998, the world's tallest building has been located in Asia. Malaysia's Petronas Towers kicked things off, followed by Taiwan's Taipei 101, and now Dubai's Burj Khalifa. The world's tallest building has grown from a height of 700 feet in 1909 to 2,717 feet today--nearly four times taller in just over a century. ## Texas GOP Senate Showdown Today
Texas Republicans head to the polls today to settle one of the most-watched Senate races of the 2026 cycle--a runoff between four-term incumbent [Sen. John Cornyn](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykUD2u4yAQPg3usGAA81xQbOMu225pYRhsJAIRkDi5_cq5wutG8-n7_XdbbzammPe_9o6mv0NZM54tYe9YV1dSwh3PUpNvWCO27-meKzCYKFMUptXbmD6rHLzZmJ_5gIZrPetZCKGGw8zhhzupPHLnfNBC201vHDcvlRCocIjmEmMKJs4ZcBhn5RTTfPthYCfpgEiGPvZSx35gx7dtIX3KC-voyn1I5uj90Yj4Q2AhsJznObqtXS0unMDypRBYrheBxZWaP5mGuB895p0-7LuXTOszlxCooiDpFYjAMlTjH2dMKbZJE8n2u43pa9p_N9XLwP8AAAD__4zNfjI) and Attorney General Ken Paxton. disclaimer_text: paid for by Joe Jaworski Campaign
body:
I do not fold. I do not trim my beliefs to fit the political winds. And I will never compromise when Texans’ rights and freedoms are on the line. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jaworskifortexas.com/last-night-14195049?e=5d8d80652b)

| | , **Today, Texas Democrats decide who we are going to send into the fight.** This campaign has never been about ambition for me. It has been about duty. My conscience compels me to stand up and use the law to fight for the people of Texas at a moment when so much feels broken, corrupted, and cruel. For months now, I have traveled this state nonstop. I have listened to Texans who are exhausted by the meanness in our politics, the corruption in our government, and the feeling that powerful people keep rigging the system against everybody else. **I am running because I believe the Attorney General should fight for working families, not corporate insiders.** I believe voting should be easier, not harder. I believe the Constitution matters. I believe no one is above the law. And I believe Democrats deserve a nominee who will not compromise with MAGA extremism or try to “manage” it politely while our rights and freedoms are under attack. I know how to fight these people because I already have. As Mayor of Galveston, I stood against racists and bullies to rebuild first-class public housing for working families after Hurricane Ike. It cost me politically, but I did it anyway because it was right. As a lawyer, I have spent 35 years standing up to powerful interests and fighting for justice in courtrooms across Texas. I sued the Governor’s handpicked UT Regents after they illegally fired thousands of workers after Hurricane Ike. I won and saved 3,800 jobs at UTMB. That is who I am. **I do not fold. I do not trim my beliefs to fit the political winds. And I will never compromise when Texans’ rights and freedoms are on the line.** Today, you have a choice. You can choose a cautious politician who talks about fighting, or you can choose a proven fighter who already has. If you believe Texas deserves an Attorney General who will tell the truth, fight corruption, defend democracy, and stand with working people every single day, then I humbly ask for your vote. **Polls are open until 7:00pm. Please get out to vote and help us finish strong.** Onward,

**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The Virginia Supreme Court just struck down the new congressional map that Virginia voters passed last month. [**So, our race just became even more crucial to our battle for the House Majority. Before I get into my background and how I’m fighting back, will you split a $25 donation to flip VA-02?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11036?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.26_Luria-Chutzpah_B1_F1_S15_C15_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=5&akid=2364%2E259176%2EJ4vNKA) | [DONATE $25](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11036?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.26_Luria-Chutzpah_B1_F1_S15_C15_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=6&akid=2364%2E259176%2EJ4vNKA)
---
_Chutzpah_ — is a Yiddish term that means _guts_ or _courage._
In 1906, my great-grandfather left his home in Poland, made the long journey through Europe and across the Atlantic, and landed in Jasper, Alabama.
That took some serious _chutzpah._
My great-grandfather believed so strongly in the promise of America – a place where he could be Jewish without fear, where he could forge his own path – that he left his whole world behind.
That promise came true for him. He built a life, a family, and a proud community.
That’s what sets America apart, Peter. Here, anyone with a little _chutzpah_ is free to be whoever they want to be, do whatever they want to do, and achieve more than they ever dreamed.
In 1993, I joined the Navy to defend those freedoms.
In 2018, I ran for Congress to expand them.
In 2020, I won re-election to continue that work, making our nation free, safe, and prosperous.
In 2022, I served on the January 6th Committee because our Constitutional freedoms were threatened.
In 2026, I’m running for Congress again, because our current representative either _can’t_ or _won’t_ protect them.
The fact is that Coastal Virginia is in crisis. Our community’s been hit hard by this president’s failed agenda. **It’s time for action.**
Flipping Virginia’s Second District won’t be easy. Dark money groups and super PACs are watching closely, trying to see if we’re strong enough to pose a real threat. **This will be one of the toughest fights of the 2026 election cycle.**
Luckily, _chutzpah_ runs in my family. I’m not afraid of a little _mishigas._ And with you behind me, I’m ready to be the unapologetic champion Virginia families need.
[**Will you split a $25 donation between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help me win this battleground race and restore America’s promise for ALL?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11036?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.05.26_Luria-Chutzpah_B1_F1_S15_C15_90AC-365DON_RS-T0&t=7&akid=2364%2E259176%2EJ4vNKA)

My great-grandfather believed so strongly in the promise of America – a place where he could be Jewish without fear, where he could forge his own path – that he left his whole world behind. That promise came true for him. He built a life, a family, and a proud community. That’s what sets America apart, Peter. Here, anyone with a little chutzpah is free to be whoever they want to be, do whatever they want to do, and achieve more than they ever dreamed. In 1993, I joined the Navy to defend those freedoms. In 2018, I ran for Congress to expand them. In 2020, I won re-election to continue that work, making our nation free, safe, and prosperous. In 2022, I served on the January 6th Committee because our Constitutional freedoms were threatened. In 2026, I’m running for Congress again, because our current representative either can’t or won’t protect them. The fact is that Coastal Virginia is in crisis. Our community’s been hit hard by this president’s failed agenda. It’s time for action. Flipping Virginia’s Second District won’t be easy. Dark money groups and super PACs are watching closely, trying to see if we’re strong enough to pose a real threat. This will be one of the toughest fights of the 2026 election cycle. Luckily, chutzpah runs in my family. I’m not afraid of a little mishigas. And with you behind me, I’m ready to be the unapologetic champion Virginia families need. [
---
See, I get why some folks voted for Trump. He promised to attack a broken system. And it’s a ripe target. Even before Trump came on the scene, America had one of the most corrupt political systems in the Western world. It’s been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money. And it’s worse than ever now. _Citizens United_ was the worst court decision in modern American history. When members of Congress aren’t begging for money from Washington lobbyists, they’re trying to dodge getting carpet-bombed by super PACs. Senators get threatened with millions of dollars of attack ads over the votes they take. And see, _that_ is why things don’t work for ordinary people. It’s because the people’s elected representatives don’t represent the people. They represent the big donors! _That corruption is why they defunded nursing homes to cut taxes for the rich._ _Corruption is why you pay a fortune for prescriptions._ _Corruption is why your insurance claim keeps getting denied._ _Corruption is why hedge funds get to buy up all the houses in your neighborhood, and then your corporate landlord ignores your calls during a gas leak._ _Corruption is why that ambulance costs $3,000 after you just had to get your choking toddler to the hospital._ Yes, the system really is rigged. But Trump’s not unrigging it. He’s re-rigging it for himself! He’s a crook and a con man, and he wants to be a king. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund their hospitals and nursing homes. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund school lunch programs to help feed little boys and little girls whose hard-working parents are struggling to fill the fridge. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you do these things so you can cut taxes for the richest people in the country while you and your family business rake in massive sums from around the world. Donald Trump’s second term has already done unfathomable damage to our country and the lives of millions of people. And the people are beginning to see it. But only by regaining Congressional power can we stop him. _Really._ The upcoming 2026 midterms are our last chance to restore checks and balances. And my Senate race in Georgia is the single most critical contest: _I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in 2026 in a state Trump carried in 2024._ **[So if you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight for the future of this Republic –– please don’t wait until 2028: Rush $5 to my reelection campaign in Georgia right now.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-may26.KE07xH&refcode=em260526-1-f&t=3&akid=2295%2E5691347%2EFIPikc) Here’s the link to donate: **[https://act.electjon.com/go/donate](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-may26.KE07xH&refcode=em260526-1-f&t=4&akid=2295%2E5691347%2EFIPikc)** The average online donation to our campaign is around $30. Please give what you can. Joining Steve is Actor, singer, dancer and writer Johnathan Zabawa who has performed in feature films, television, commercials and theater. Johnathan has been a lead singer of multiple bands that have performed around the country. He began performing at a young age and has continued since his move to Los Angles in 2003. That same year, he began working for the iconic Debbie Reynolds, who gave him the greatest gift ever: an entertainers education of a lifetime! For the next 15 years, John was a major part of the world-famous Debbie Reynolds Studio in North Hollywood, CA, where he was fortunate to witness countless stars rehearse for their performances in acting, dancing, and music. He has worked with multiple stars, including Debbie Reynolds, Carrie Fisher, Arthur Duncan, Catherine Hickland, and Annie Semler. For more about Johnathan visit
https://zabawa.live/

Debbie Reynolds will be remembered as America's Sweetheart,' star of 'Singin' in The Rain,' best-selling author and an Academy Award nominee for her leading role in 'The Unsinkable Molly Brown.' Debbie's career spanned more than 60 years, not to mention her vast collection of Hollywood memorabilia. Carrie Fisher cofounder of the studio became a household name for playing Princess Leia in the Star Wars movie franchise. For more about Debbie Reynolds Studio visit

subject: Urgent update from public broadcasting CEO

body:
An unexpected setback.
| Our fight is FAR FROM OVER: [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/109904?t=6&akid=24499%2E878179%2EUCUo4-) A judge recently DEMANDED Trump resume funding for public broadcasting networks — but he STILL hasn’t acted and public media is STILL underwater.

**If we don’t act FAST, we could lose these critical networks for good!**

[**Public broadcasters need to know we have their backs! So we’re gathering 10,000 signatures by MIDNIGHT to stay in the fight and show our solidarity »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/109904?t=7&akid=24499%2E878179%2EUCUo4-) | [**Chip in $3 to sign now »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/109904?t=8&akid=24499%2E878179%2EUCUo4-)
---
TO: Public Broadcasters
FROM: A grateful Democrat
Subject: Thank you! To all public broadcasters,

Thank you. Thank you for enriching all of our lives — in rural and urban areas, and everywhere in between — with your various news and educational programs.

I couldn’t be more THRILLED to see Trump’s disgusting executive order blocked. _His authoritarian power grab didn’t stand a chance against our fight._

**But until your funding is resumed, I won’t stop fighting. I also know that his attempts to SILENCE the free press won’t end here.**

It’s not just upsetting, _it’s a dangerous step towards an**outright dictatorship!**_ That’s why I’m not getting complacent.

[**I’m signing this letter today by chipping in $3 to VPP to thank you for your years of service and to join VPP in the fight against Trump’s attacks on the free press. It is absolutely critical that we elect more good Democrats who defend public media and our most essential freedoms »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/109904?t=9&akid=24499%2E878179%2EUCUo4-) | [**Chip in $3 to sign now »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/109904?t=10&akid=24499%2E878179%2EUCUo4-)

Patriot,

The radical Left and the Fake News Media want you to believe that the people who were at the Capitol on January are all criminals and terrorists.

These people are fathers, mothers, sons, daughters, sisters, brothers, friends, patriots, and neighbors. **They are also the victims of a heinous propaganda campaign.**

While the pardons freed us from criminal legal consequences, they don’t restore mental health, family ties, or livelihoods. They don’t erase the trauma, stigma, barriers, or burdens we face.

**I started Stand in the Gap because I believe these patriots deserve a second chance, so we’re giving them the help they need to get back on their feet.**

* Help finding a place to live or covering the down payment on a place to rent.
* Assistance with an electric bill or car repair.
* Relief from a medical bill caused by their time behind bars.
* Covering the cost of a transcript required to appeal their cases.

These are the kinds of emergencies Stand in the Gap deals with every single week.

But they don’t need them to make a difference, because they have you.

Even if you find that you’re unable to give, prayers are always much appreciated.

Thank you for your time, consideration, and support.

Shane Jenkins

body:
Please watch and share:

**This is a corruption story -- theft at a grand scale.**
What Donald Trump does is to scapegoat teachers, scapegoat immigrants, scapegoat the book you're reading and get us to fight one another while he picks everyone's pocket.
💰 $1.8 billion for a slush fund to hand out to insurrectionists, oath keepers, proud boys and whoever else he wants.
🏰 The $1 billion ballroom he wants to build for himself.
📈 Look at his stock portfolio and trades -- when he's buying stock before he shows up at a factory and says the words he needs to say in order for that stock to spike.
🏨 Look at the eight large scale projects he has in the Gulf and around the globe. The fact that he used the tariffs to get those deals done, particularly the one in Vietnam.
⌚️ The crypto, the watches, the cell phones, the sneakers... what he's doing across the spectrum ... it's sick.
This is happening at a scale we've never seen before and he is just winding up.
**[Please watch and share:](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/7931?t=1&akid=2951%2E4767699%2EZVwAFQ)**
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/7931?t=2&akid=2951%2E4767699%2EZVwAFQ)
The good news is: we have agency and a responsibility. It's just like the issue of redistricting.
We could have decided to write an op-ed, hold hands, have a candlelight vigil and win the argument.
Yes, it's uncomfortable fighting fire with fire. Yes, we all want the better angels and the Sorkin West Wing resolutions.
We all do...
But we will lose our country if we do not fight back.
Thanks for being in the fight with me,
Gavin Newsom

# Conforti Grassroots Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

Welcome to our interactive grassroots newsletter. As we approach the Midterm Election 2026, this newsletter is dedicated to keeping the hardworking constituents of Illinois' 6th Congressional District informed and engaged.

Our campaign is built on a "district-first" mentality. We are committed to prioritizing your needs, focusing on fundamental ideals of sensible solutions and open dialogue. Through this newsletter, we will provide you with regular updates on policy, campaign events, and current community events happening right here in our district.
Click the button below to make a donation today. Your donations are what makes this possible.
---

| |

| |
## Kitchen Table Tuesday.
The Conforti Brief.
District-First Events.
---
| |
### Educate. Inform. Invite.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
# Kitchen Table Tuesday
---
| | **Educating and connecting** with voters on important issues.
---
| | |
---
| | Right now, families across Illinois' 6th District are feeling the pressure, and **high energy costs** are identified as a primary driver of the current high cost-of-living in our district. As an energy consultant, I understand exactly why this is happening and how to fix it. The burden of overregulation is stifling our energy sector, driving up prices and making life harder for everyday citizens. We need a common-sense approach that prioritizes affordability and reliability for our community.
.To provide immediate relief, my goal in Congress is to propose legislation that cuts regulations in the energy industry and limits the renewable energy component. By adopting this "speed to power" approach, we can make our energy grid significantly more resilient and, most importantly, **more affordable for local households**. It is time to ease the financial pressure on our constituents and ensure that hard-working families don't have to break the bank just to keep the lights on.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| | The Threat to Fair Play: Protecting Title IX in Women's Sports
Recently, Yahoo Sports reported on a controversial incident involving a transgender high school track athlete competing in the girls' division, sparking a nationwide debate over **fairness in athletics**. This situation highlights a growing concern that is deeply felt by families right here in Illinois' 6th Congressional District.
For decades, female athletes have **worked tirelessly to achieve equality** , making it a matter of protecting the important rights owed to women under Title IX. Unfortunately, Democrats, like my opponent Sean Casten, are pushing an agenda that is directly in opposition with the values of his constituents. We must guarantee that these hard-won opportunities are preserved, which is why I firmly believe that women athletes deserve to compete on a fair playing field.
As your candidate for Illinois' 6th Congressional District, **I support equal opportunities for women** —which means women athletes deserve to compete without being forced to play against biological males.
When elected to represent the 6th District in the U.S. House of Representatives, I will take direct action to address this issue by:

1. 1\. **Supporting the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act:** I will proudly support S.9, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025. This crucial legislation will provide positive protections and ensure that the integrity of women's sports is maintained.2\. **Defending Title IX:** I will work to ensure that the important rights owed to women athletes in Title IX of the Education Amendments are fiercely protected.
2. 3\. **Ensuring Fair Competition:** I will fight to guarantee that every young woman in our district has the chance to compete, excel, and be recognized fairly for her dedication and hard work.

Children are our future, and we must protect them. It is time to ensure equality is based on a fair playing field.

Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://conforti4congress.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7fd34b7284bf7f5e87a4e45e5&id=dc9a9ae7cf&e=25f4fa3311)

# District-First
# Events
---
| | **Inviting voters** to community events and how they can get involved!**
**Join the Conforti Campaign at the**Darien Town Hall Event!**
---
| |
---
| | We warmly invite you to participate and join Niki Conforti and our campaign team at our upcoming Town Hall! Come out to show your support for our "district-first" mentality and join the community for this important occasion. This town hall is an opportunity to discuss our campaign's focus on fundamental ideals like community safety, the cost-of-living crisis, and the run-away national debt.

* **Date:** Wednesday, June 17th
* **Time:** 6:30 PM - 7:30 PM
* **Location:** Indian Prairie Library in Darien, IL (401 Plainfield Rd, Darien, IL 60561)
*
Bring your family, friends, and neighbors to join us as we share Niki's platform of sensible solutions, economic affordability, and community safety with the voters of the 6th District. As a candidate for Illinois' 6th Congressional District, Niki is committed to prioritizing your needs.
We would love to have you join our ranks for this special day! To get more details, please contact our team at [**info@conforti4congress.com**](mailto:info@conforti4congress.com?subject=Event%3A%20Darien%20Town%20Hall&body=).

We look forward to seeing you there!

Good morning, Peter.
My name is Adam Kinzinger. You might know me as one of the only Republicans in Congress on the January 6th Committee, and one of 10 Republicans who voted to impeach Trump.
I’ll be straight with you — I’m a proud conservative. But I am going to do what I can to help elect Alex Vindman to the U.S. Senate in Florida this November. Our democracy is more important than parties or politics.
Alex and I are both veterans.
I served this country flying KC-135s and RC-26Bs with multiple tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, and Alex was a 21-year U.S. Army combat veteran who was wounded in Iraq and awarded a Purple Heart.
Both of us took an oath to the Constitution and defended our democracy and fundamental rights with everything we had.
Alex and I may not agree on everything, but I fully trust him to tell the truth, to protect our freedoms, and to work for the best interests of Floridians and all Americans.
But it is going to take all of us doing our part to get him there. And right now, the most important thing you could possibly do to help is to make a contribution to his campaign. These early contributions are worth their weight in gold.
So I am asking:
[**Can you please make a contribution to Alex Vindman's campaign for U.S. Senate in Florida? His average online contribution is around $30. Many give more. Some give less. No amount is too small. It all adds up fast when so many people are chipping in to help elect Alex.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q22026?refcode=em260524-ob&refcode2=565_3892029_gK9ia1&akid=565%2E3892029%2EgK9ia1)

| Peter,
On Election Day, the phones at Louisiana Democratic Party headquarters in Baton Rouge started ringing at 6 a.m. and never stopped.
Hundreds of calls flooded our voter protection hotline from across the state during last Saturday's primary elections. The calls described the same story over and over: requesting a Democratic ballot but receiving a Republican ballot, voters unable to cast a ballot in the Senate primary, No Party voters receiving the incorrect forms to fill out, and many voters leaving polling locations altogether because they were so frustrated with the process.
This chaos was not an accident. As one LSU political scientist put it, Governor Landry created a system that was "almost designed in a lab to discourage people from participating in the electoral process." Our own executive director Dadrius Lanus called it what it was: voter suppression and voter intimidation.
This is what MAGA control of Louisiana elections looks like.
---

After this fiasco, we also need to expand the amount of poll watchers and volunteers on the ground who can report issues at polling locations back to our headquarters immediately on Election Day. No Louisiana voter should ever walk away from a polling place without their ballot being counted.
But we cannot do this alone. The Louisiana Democratic Party is one of the most underfunded state parties in the nation. Hi Peter -- Right now, too many Mainers are struggling.

I hear it everywhere I go. Young people can’t afford to live near their jobs or families. Energy costs keep rising. Child care is hard to find. And too many hardworking people feel like they’re doing everything right but still falling behind.

**It doesn’t have to be this way.**

We can build more housing and help first-time homebuyers. We can lower energy costs by changing where we get our power and how ratepayers are charged. We can create a more predictable environment for businesses so they can grow and create good-paying jobs here in Maine.

**But to get there, we need leadership focused on practical solutions – not partisan talking points.**

That’s why I’m asking for your help right now.

Our May 26 finance reporting deadline is at midnight tonight, and every contribution helps us reach more Maine people with a message focused on results, integrity, and common sense.

**[If you believe Maine needs a different kind of leadership, can you make a contribution before midnight tonight?](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/donate?e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=may26&n=1)**

Together, we can build a Maine where hard work leads to opportunity.

Let’s get to work.

Rick

### 6 American Heroes You Never Learned About in School
---
| |
---
| | Whenever Memorial Day rolls around, we look forward to a long weekend — hopefully with a sun-drenched cookout and precious time with family and friends. If we're not careful, though, it's very easy to miss the heart of this all-American holiday. Do have the cookout, and by all means, sleep in on Monday. But please, don't forget the many thousands of heroes who gave everything for our nation, their families, and every future American generation. We want to help this week by remembering a few courageous men whose stories should be told and retold as we commemorate their lives and heroism:🇺🇸 Navy SEAL, PO2, Michael A. Monsoor – Operation Iraqi Freedom🇺🇸 PFC Lewis Albanese – Vietnam War🇺🇸 Cpl. Desmond Doss – World War II🇺🇸 Cpt. Mervyn Bennion – Pearl Harbor🇺🇸 Sgt. Henry Johnson – World War I🇺🇸 James Armistead Lafayette – American Spy – Revolutionary War Their stories deserve to be remembered — not just today, but by every generation that follows. Read the full blog to learn more about these remarkable heroes by joining our free Moms TownSquare membership.

# Raising the Parents of Tomorrow
---
| |
---
| | What if parenting is about more than raising good kids? What if the real mission is raising the future mothers and fathers who will shape the next generation — and the one after that? That's the powerful idea at the heart of this week's episode, and it just might change the way you see your role as a parent. We sit down with Pastor Jonathan Brozozog — pastor of Creative Church in Minneapolis, author, speaker, coach, and father of eight — to explore the transformative message behind his book Raising Parents: Set Your Kids Up for Future Success. A true conservative is not simply someone who votes a certain way or aligns with a political party.

He served as a high-level climate advisor in both the Obama and Biden administrations, helping shape national climate strategy at the highest levels of government.
Earlier in his career, he helped launch the California Climate Action Corps, putting young people to work tackling the climate crisis head-on. And he's helped design nationally recognized climate justice laws.
Everywhere he's worked, Jake's focus has been to make government move faster, think bigger, and treat the climate crisis like the emergency it is.
**But what moves me most about Jake isn't his résumé. It's that he knows personally what a climate disaster feels like.**
Last year, Jake's mother lost her home in the Palisades Fire. Since then, he's returned to LA and has been working with nonprofits on fire recovery alongside the very families now rebuilding their lives.
He’s lived through the heartbreak and devastation that thousands of California families are facing right now. He knows what's at stake. And I know he'll fight like hell for our planet and every person who calls this beautiful place home.
**[We need bold champions in Washington willing to fight hard and treat the climate crisis like the emergency it is. Jake is one of them — but only if we get him through this primary first. clean_body: Meet the climate champion JanePAC just endorsed for Congress. | In one week, voters in my home state of California will head to the polls in one of the most consequential primaries of 2026. California's 32nd Congressional District will decide whether we send a new generation of climate leadership to Congress — or hand another two years to a 15-term incumbent who treats climate like a checkbox. That's why JanePAC is proud to endorse Jake Levine for Congress in CA-32. = Jake is running in a crowded, competitive primary against 15-term incumbent Brad Sherman because he believes CA-32 deserves to be a true CLIMATE seat, represented by someone who understands the urgency of this crisis personally and professionally. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Jake has spent his career proving that climate leadership can’t just live in speeches or policy papers — it has to change people’s lives. He served as a high-level climate advisor in both the Obama and Biden administrations, helping shape national climate strategy at the highest levels of government. Earlier in his career, he helped launch the California Climate Action Corps, putting young people to work tackling the climate crisis head-on. And he's helped design nationally recognized climate justice laws. Everywhere he's worked, Jake's focus has been to make government move faster, think bigger, and treat the climate crisis like the emergency it is. But what moves me most about Jake isn't his résumé. It's that he knows personally what a climate disaster feels like. Last year, Jake's mother lost her home in the Palisades Fire. Since then, he's returned to LA and has been working with nonprofits on fire recovery alongside the very families now rebuilding their lives. He’s lived through the heartbreak and devastation that thousands of California families are facing right now. He knows what's at stake. And I know he'll fight like hell for our planet and every person who calls this beautiful place home. = In solidarity, xx Jane = | Follow along: | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. Jane Fonda Climate PAC 600 Pennsylvania Ave SE #15180 Washington, DC 20003 United States

One week ago today was the Pennsylvania primary.
It was supposed to be a great day, not just for me but for my family.
My mom was scheduled to get a surgery that very day that would vastly improve her quality of life as she battled with Parkinson's disease.
Halfway through Tuesday, it was clear that something about the surgery went wrong. We pulled down campaign stops for the rest of the day. But when we were told that she still hadn't woken up after the surgery, I went to Philadelphia to tell her myself that she needed to wake up.
She never did. And on Friday, [my mom passed away.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2c6c9111-0406-4ea9-86cc-c149b721bc56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
My family is in shock, but we are together. And that is half the battle.
For now, the most important thing I can do is be with the people I love, and so I'm taking some time away from the campaign trail.
Thank you to everyone who has prayed for my mom - and please keep my family in your prayers.

May 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- One week ago today was the Pennsylvania primary. It was supposed to be a great day, not just for me but for my family. My mom was scheduled to get a surgery that very day that would vastly improve her quality of life as she battled with Parkinson's disease. Halfway through Tuesday, it was clear that something about the surgery went wrong. We pulled down campaign stops for the rest of the day. But when we were told that she still hadn't woken up after the surgery, I went to Philadelphia to tell her myself that she needed to wake up. She never did. And on Friday, My family is in shock, but we are together. And that is half the battle. For now, the most important thing I can do is be with the people I love, and so I'm taking some time away from the campaign trail. Earlier this year, I got the chance to call David – one of this campaign’s thousands of grassroots donors – and thank him for his support. He told me he’s “in it all the way,” and ready to vote in the midterms. Check out this video about our conversation → [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132099321/623389964/935561440?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_CallCampaign_260526_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMzRmOWY5My0xMzU5LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QOxOFJOXWjNX1PojWLJ7lZFuHxgvowFWyihw4UQ0X28=) Look, I’m running this race the same way I’ve always run – getting out and meeting voters, talking about the issues facing Virginians, and humbling asking folks to rehire me.

**A huge part of that effort is thanking grassroots supporters like you for the time, energy, and hard-earned dollars you give to this campaign.** That’s why I’ve asked my team to once again select a few grassroots donors for me to call and personally thank them for their support.

[_**So, can you chip in your first $5 donation to my reelection campaign? If you do, you might get a call from me thanking you for your donation.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132099322/623389967/935561440?amount=5&refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_CallCampaign_260526_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMzRmOWY5My0xMzU5LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QOxOFJOXWjNX1PojWLJ7lZFuHxgvowFWyihw4UQ0X28=)

Look, I know the constant chaos and cruelty coming out of this administration is exhausting. The president’s war-of-choice is raising prices at the pump. Republicans across the country are rigging congressional maps in their favor. And too few of my Republican colleagues are willing to speak out or push back on this insanity.

**This November, Virginia can turn the tide. We can defend this Senate seat and flip House seats across the Commonwealth. We can elect Democrats who will finally put a check on Trump’s dangerous agenda and stand up for working families.**

[_**But that’s only possible if we have the resources to compete, organize, and win big. That’s why I’m asking you to pitch in to this campaign today. Can I count on you? And as a reminder, if you donate today, you just might see me in your call list.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132099323/623389970/935561440?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_CallCampaign_260526_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMzRmOWY5My0xMzU5LWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExODkwNWMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QOxOFJOXWjNX1PojWLJ7lZFuHxgvowFWyihw4UQ0X28=)

Whether you can give today or not, please know how thankful I am to have you by my side, in this fight.

On Memorial Day, as the nation pauses to honor those who made the ultimate sacrifice for freedom, my thoughts turn to Fred Fillbrook, a remarkable figure whose life embodied service, community, and resilience. A proud veteran of the U.S. Army's 82nd Airborne Division and the founder of the Mill Creek View newspaper in Mill Creek, Washington, Fillbrook's legacy resonates deeply, especially on this solemn day of remembrance.
Fred Fillbrook's journey began in Detroit, Michigan, where he was born in 1937. At 18, he joined the Army, driven by a sense of duty that had been shaped by his family's military history. His service with the 82nd Airborne, an elite paratrooper unit, took him to Fort Bragg, North Carolina, for jump school and later to Fort Sherman in Panama for jungle warfare training. Fillbrook completed 38 jumps, a testament to his courage and commitment. His military experience was not just a chapter in his life but a cornerstone of his identity, reflected in his lifelong dedication to honoring veterans. Memorial Day, for Fillbrook, was more than a holiday; it was a call to remember those, like his uncle Jack Rogers and cousin who died during World War II, who never returned home.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=199336794&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk5MzM2Nzk0LCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk4MDgyODAsImV4cCI6MTc4MjQwMDI4MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.3z8pQQbdlXBKUn-4t_ekPy_HZ6OvbqO4oYSh61w8dUI)
After his active duty and eight years in the Army Reserve, Fillbrook settled in Mill Creek, Washington, where he left an indelible mark on the community. In 1991, he founded the Mill Creek View, a biweekly newspaper that became a vital voice for local news and stories. As publisher and senior editor, Fillbrook championed transparency and community engagement, even when it sparked controversy, as seen in his 1995 lawsuit against a rival paper over a disputed article. His commitment to truth and integrity in journalism mirrored the discipline he carried from his military days.

Fillbrook's passion for veterans' recognition shone brightly in Mill Creek. He co-founded the city's Veterans Day Parade, revitalizing a tradition he felt had been overlooked, and co-established the Veterans Monument in Library Park, where names of his ancestors are etched. These efforts ensured that the sacrifices of service members were never forgotten. On Memorial Day, I imagine Fillbrook at the monument, camera in hand, capturing moments of reverence during the annual ceremony, which he helped shape into a community touchstone.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.eWjcj3uLNs_7hD1_4ZMzYkr1cjHik5UjiP0RBwap-tM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=199336794)
His contributions extended beyond veterans' advocacy. Fillbrook was a community activist, a member of Amvets and the American Legion, and even a karaoke enthusiast, bringing joy to those around him. When he passed away in February 2022 at 85, the Kiwanis Club and Mill Creek Chamber of Commerce dedicated a memorial bench to him at The Forum on Main Street, a fitting tribute to a man who worked tirelessly to make Mill Creek a place of pride.

This Memorial Day, as I reflect on Fred Fillbrook, I'm reminded of the power of one individual's dedication. His service in the 82nd Airborne, his stewardship of the Mill Creek View, and his devotion to honoring fallen heroes embody the spirit of this day. Fillbrook's life challenges us to remember, to serve, and to build communities that uphold the values for which so many gave everything.

AP: Trump casts Florida mail ballot as he pushes Congress to severely limit that voting option [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=052626_1&amount=25]
Team: Donald Trump voted by mail. No, we're not referring to his well-documented past usage of the practice.
No, after years of attacking vote-by-mail, countless late-night Truth Social rants, and several executive orders within the last year trying to end, or at least curtail, mail-in voting, Donald Trump voted by mail this spring, in a Florida special election held on March 24, 2026 . He could have gone to an early voting site when he was at Mar-A-Lago the week before the election, but he chose to submit a mailed ballot instead, according to Palm Beach County voter records.
To be honest, we here at Voter Action Project are glad he did. We believe every eligible American deserves to vote in the manner that is easiest for them to participate. That's because we believe that the act of participation is the most important part, not what method you use to cast your ballot.
It's worth noting, however, how he's very willing to use this tool to help himself and make his own voice heard, but he wants to restrict it for everyone else if it seems like it might not benefit him. The pattern is completely clear, and his self-interest drives every decision and statement he makes about voting.
So next time you run into that anti-voting family member, friend, or neighbor who hates mail-in voting, just let them know: Trump himself chose to skip voting in person while in Florida and voted by mail in 2026.
Onward,
The Voter Action Project Team

No, we're not referring to his well-documented past usage of the practice. No, after years of attacking vote-by-mail, countless late-night Truth Social rants, and several executive orders within the last year trying to end, or at least curtail, mail-in voting, Donald Trump voted by mail this spring, in a Florida special election held on March 24, 2026 . He could have gone to an early voting site when he was at Mar-A-Lago the week before the election, but he chose to submit a mailed ballot instead, according to Palm Beach County voter records. To be honest, we here at Voter Action Project are glad he did. We believe every eligible American deserves to vote in the manner that is easiest for them to participate. That's because we believe that the act of participation is the most important part, not what method you use to cast your ballot. It's worth noting, however, how he's very willing to use this tool to help himself and make his own voice heard, but he wants to restrict it for everyone else if it seems like it might not benefit him. The pattern is completely clear, and his self-interest drives every decision and statement he makes about voting. So next time you run into that anti-voting family member, friend, or neighbor who hates mail-in voting, just let them know: Trump himself chose to skip voting in person while in Florida and voted by mail in 2026. In January of 2024, the Mississippi Legislature voted in a special session to strip the Public Service Commission of its normal advance-approval authority over new electric generation, so that Entergy Mississippi could build power plants for Amazon Web Services without going through the standard regulatory front door. In April of 2026, Entergy and Mississippi Power are now asking that same Public Service Commission to use its full advance-approval authority to stop a competitor from building its own power plant for its own data center.
Same agency. Same statute. Two completely opposite requests. Both made in the favor of the same two established power companies.
If you want to understand what is wrong with the way Mississippi regulates this industry, you do not need to look any further than that pair of facts.
Start with what the legislature did in 2024. Senate Bill 2001 of the 2024 Second Extraordinary Session, signed by Governor Reeves on January 30 of that year, passed the Senate 49 to 1 and the House 120 to 2. Among other things, it authorized Entergy to build new power generating facilities tied to the AWS project without first obtaining the PSC's normal Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity. The PSC kept the authority to set rates and to review costs after the fact for prudence. But the upfront question of whether this generation should be built at all, and on whose dime, was taken off the PSC's desk and handed to Entergy and the company they were building for. The justification at the time was that the standard process would slow the deal down and risk losing AWS to another state.
Now turn to 2026. In April, a Jackson-area developer named Gabriel Prado, the man behind the Fondren luxury apartments and the Topgolf in Ridgeland, filed Mississippi PSC Docket 2026-AD-10. He is asking the PSC for a declaratory opinion that he is not a public utility and does not need a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity to build a 350 megawatt natural gas plant in Ridgeland. The plant would exclusively power his own on-site project, a data center and an AI semiconductor fabrication facility. He is not proposing to sell power on the open market. He is not asking the State of Mississippi for a $44 million workforce training appropriation, a $215 million local infrastructure loan, or a 30 year rolling tax exemption. He is proposing to build it with private capital, on his own land, for his own use.
Entergy filed in opposition on April 13. Mississippi Power filed shortly after. Both companies argue that even though Prado would only be serving the tenants of his own campus, he should be classified as a public utility, because Ridgeland sits inside Entergy's state certificated service area, where Entergy holds an exclusive right to sell power. They are leaning, according to Mississippi Today's reporting, on a 2024 amendment to the Mississippi Public Utilities Act that expanded the definition of serving "the public" to explicitly include "an individual person or an entity or a collection of persons or entities." In their formal filing, Entergy argues that whether Prado's customers are "individual person(s) or an entity or a collection of persons ... they meet the definition of the public."
Read those two episodes side by side and the pattern is unmistakable. When the regulatory framework would have slowed AWS down, the legislature waived it. When the same regulatory framework can be deployed against a new entrant who would compete with the established utilities, those utilities are now invoking it. The agency in the middle, our Public Service Commission, is being asked to apply two different rules to two different developers, with the difference between them being which one is already on the inside.
That is not deregulation. That is not free market policy. That is exactly what the academic chapter by Garrett and Shughart in Promoting Prosperity in Mississippi calls "crony capitalism." It is a regulatory framework that produces benefits for politically connected firms and costs for everyone who is not in the room when the rules are being written.
The Mississippi conservative position on this should not be complicated. Either the Public Service Commission has full advance approval authority over new electric generation tied to data centers, applied equally to Entergy, to Prado AI Industrial, and to anyone else who walks in the door, or it does not. Whichever rule we pick, it has to be the rule for everyone. Selective application of regulation, with the line drawn around who happens to already be a customer of the State of Mississippi's economic development office, is the textbook definition of regulatory capture. Conservatives have been writing about its dangers since at least Adam Smith.
There is a clock on this. The PSC's Public Utilities Staff is due to file its input in the Prado docket by May 15. The Commission has indicated it will issue its opinion by June 1. Mississippians who care about this should call our three elected commissioners and say it plainly: do not give Entergy one set of rules and Prado another. Apply the law equally.
If the PSC blocks Prado with rules the Legislature waived for Entergy, every Mississippi developer with private capital will hear the message clearly: do not bother. The deck is stacked.
That is not how a state attracts the next generation of investment. That is how a state protects the insiders, punishes the outsiders, and asks the rest of us to pay the bill.

clean_body: Mississippi Crony Capitalism on Display | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? from the desk ofDana Criswell Mississippi Crony Capitalism on Display | | | May 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- In January of 2024, the Mississippi Legislature voted in a special session to strip the Public Service Commission of its normal advance-approval authority over new electric generation, so that Entergy Mississippi could build power plants for Amazon Web Services without going through the standard regulatory front door. If you want to understand what is wrong with the way Mississippi regulates this industry, you do not need to look any further than that pair of facts. Start with what the legislature did in 2024. Senate Bill 2001 of the 2024 Second Extraordinary Session, signed by Governor Reeves on January 30 of that year, passed the Senate 49 to 1 and the House 120 to 2. Among other things, it authorized Entergy to build new power generating facilities tied to the AWS project without first obtaining the PSC's normal Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity. The PSC kept the authority to set rates and to review costs after the fact for prudence. But the upfront question of whether this generation should be built at all, and on whose dime, was taken off the PSC's desk and handed to Entergy and the company they were building for. subject: You don’t hear from me too often… so when I reach out, you know it’s important.
