# [Donald Trump is trying to steal $1.8 billion in taxpayer money](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=199344991&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk5MzQ0OTkxLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzk4Mjk0NzgsImV4cCI6MTc4MjQyMTQ3OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kf5hHl7eMBVKCP_EFyALrAaiXg8LfRFuMGe9aEwMOx0)
### This is what corruption looks like
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| May 26
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL2RvbmFsZC10cnVtcC1pcy10cnlpbmctdG8tc3RlYWwtMTg_.gl7wUtLgg67CuuiL5hbtRTFiwTdSO-0qmGmu4iFzHQI?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/donald-trump-is-trying-to-steal-18?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Michiganders are getting crushed at the pump. They're worried about losing their health care. Their wages are flat. And too many folks are making impossible choices - buy a second bag of groceries or save that money so they can afford their kid's asthma medication.
These are not hypotheticals. This is what real people are dealing with right now.
When I saw what came out of the White House this month, I was furious.
**Because the hard truth is that the leadership in Washington right now, Donald Trump and his MAGA allies, do not work for you.**
Because if they did, they wouldn't be trying to give away $1.8 billion in taxpayer money to January 6 rioters.
Here's what's happening:
Last week, Donald Trump's Justice Department announced a brand-new fund: $1.8 billion in taxpayer money (_your money_) set aside to pay Donald Trump's political allies. They're calling it the "Anti-Weaponization Fund," which is a fancy name for what it actually is: a slush fund for MAGA friends.
And the way this came together would be funny if it weren't pure corruption. Donald Trump, as a private citizen, sued the IRS - an agency that Donald Trump, as president, oversees.
Trump's personal lawyers negotiated against Justice Department lawyers who answer to an attorney general who used to be Trump's personal lawyer.
Then they worked out a deal.
That deal shields Trump and his family from further tax exposure and creates a huge taxpayer-funded pot of money for the people Trump's team decides are deserving. The fund is set to stop paying out in December 2028 - the month before Trump's term ends.
I am not exaggerating any of this. This is a pile of taxpayer cash for the president to hand out to whoever he wants.
Friends, this is what corruption looks like. I need to say that again, because we cannot grow numb to this nonsense:
**This is what corruption looks like.**
And this is not an isolated scandal. It is part of a MAGA pattern.
And the pattern matters, because once you see it, you cannot unsee it. Look at where the money flows when Donald Trump is in charge.
His tariffs are pushing prices up at the local grocery store. His war in Iran is pushing prices up at your gas pump.
His tax bill moved money from the working people to billionaires who don't ever need a job to pay their bills.
His health care agenda is closing rural hospitals, pushing people off coverage, and making life harder for seniors on a fixed income already trying to stretch every dollar.
And now this: a $1.8 billion fund for his cronies, paid for by regular Americans.
You. Me. Every working family already getting squeezed.
Every single one of those policies takes money from regular folks and moves it somewhere else - toward Trump and his friends and his donors.
This is not an accident. This is the point. This is the Trump project.
Let me tell you what my project is, because I think it's only fair that you know exactly what I am running for.
I am running to bring down the cost of prescription drugs, because no senior should have to choose between her medication and her electric bill.
I am running to protect and expand Medicare and Medicaid and lower health insurance prices, because every Michigander deserves to see a doctor when they are sick.
I am running to actually invest in American manufacturing - not the slogans-and-tariffs version, but the real version, where we build the cars and the chips and the stuff people need right here at home.
I am running to lower energy and fuel costs for Michigan families and small businesses, because $5 gas is not some abstract talking point. It is a real burden on real people.
And I am running to fight every corrupt effort to siphon taxpayer money toward Donald Trump's friends, family, and political allies while Michigan families are told there is nothing left for them.
That's the difference. Trump's policies move money toward the folks who already have it, and the policies I am fighting for move money toward the people who actually do the work.
That is exactly the contrast that will be on the ballot in November. Because the other person running for this Senate seat, MAGA Republican Mike Rogers, has shown us exactly who he will be.
He will rubber-stamp this slush fund. And he will rubber-stamp the next one. He hasn't raised his voice as Donald Trump goes after the rule of law. Mike Rogers is not the sort of person who stands up to Donald Trump.
[But I am.](https://substack.com/redirect/600dd3b7-7c73-4e51-9cb0-3323c8329917?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**A senator from Michigan should be the strongest voice in the building for the family struggling to afford rent, the worker on the line, the senior at the pharmacy counter, and the kid in a public school.**
I'm not here for the president's right-wing friends and MAGA billionaire donors. I'm here for Michigan.
I have been my entire life. And we're just getting started.
More soon.
With grit,
Haley
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/600dd3b7-7c73-4e51-9cb0-3323c8329917?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

NC Newsline: Amid protests, NC elections board rejects campus voting sites and Sunday voting in several counties [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052626_2&amount=25]
We're facing the repercussions of the partisan election takeover laws that went into effect at the end of 2024, Team.
To refresh your memory: After the 2024 elections and the defeat of a MAGA candidate for governor, opponents of voting rights in North Carolina jammed through a bill that took the power of the governor to appoint people to election boards and handed that to the state auditor . It's worth noting that the state auditor is the only statewide elected Republican, with Democrats winning the 2024 races for governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, and secretary of state.
Now, among massive protests from young voters, the MAGA-fied North Carolina State Elections Board recently shot down proposals to continue having early voting sites at several universities around the state . These weren't new sites either; these were places where North Carolina had provided early voting locations for a decade or more.
This is voter suppression, plain and simple, by making it harder for eligible, registered voters to vote in-person by taking away their polling place. It's another demonstration of how opponents of voting rights in North Carolina are more focused on expanding and cementing their own power than they are in serving the people and having fair elections.
We have to fight these suppressive actions in North Carolina and any other state where opponents of voting rights try to replicate this. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today to help every eligible voter cast their ballot >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052626_2&amount=35]

These new, highly partisan State Election Board members wouldn't even look the protestors in the eye or engage with their proposals. After the vote, Chairman Francis De Luca threatened to call the cops on students if they didn’t leave.
Need to better understand how this impacts young voters? Western Carolina University in Jackson County, for example, has had a polling place on campus since 2016 that’s been used in five general elections and four primaries, according to a document prepared for the board. The state board voted 3-2 to get rid of it.
Closing the campus voting site would not save money, but “ would create barriers to voting for young, rural residents ,” Jackson County Board member Betsy Swift told the state board. 64% of students don’t have vehicles to drive to the polling place, she said.
Without the on-campus site, the closest polling place for students will be a recreation center nearly two miles away. Students without transportation will have to walk along a four-lane highway and through a meadow to get there.
Voter suppression isn't just black and white photos of eligible voters being turned away from polling places. Voter suppression is making it harder for eligible voters to take part in our elections through onerous ID requirements, closing polling places, taking away voting locations, or ending mail-in voting. Every time someone makes it harder to cast your ballot, voters are suppressed.

45 agonizing days under a bridge
For five years, we have done this work from temporary facilities and borrowed space, with on-the-fly logistics.

| | | | | |
---
[ ](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=051ea43747454832a3e457f7a35a64bf&_e=gIaj_jiIbQc3Uty1ysOAfmVoGxTLIiWcQmf3ypBIr2BzY2uWrk5whzwUs1xOHbqqbtm4NVW7giGcvqYinXdb-MnteMRUwarVYjGu5kGu7aWizF5a97N9rufyxBLrPzV8BNCSclsYnhZEEmIj-R-uo0Ur3NOma9VA-n22yhe7moaOpHyVyf4o8XjbQ9MsVUdE9wClwVhDc9ZNWivRcUkN589Y9a4dg_NB0Tjkd5kH8Dkch_rJCZ1mHby5RipkBQifwA93jbUDeOYvh_HtHlZCS6FZ5FyCHSbpnJO9zLezTTxDhPbmwDVDd11rC6uNPtFy1Fj3Orvm9i_vKmS9G4ikoTzrLHnvvU7RkFPZaWactCTossKRBk_x5qEOBI5CZ5Rk0afb0-tqlCYDOeo900vqYpPBA3WRQTnHpbVpBia6OjwgE9pv9Ub_c96urb-2GVxCeKDB2tvLrEn9qcUm_7XTjQqz7_7vEhbaB7rMTTOXSJ2d1G4JmKR3P3PGDiL1gIwXefiijJo9Y-Ns_-v9K8LqTuvyFZYS2CRvKtMRpyXXDyGXYTjh2XtA3oRKbMGMjXazIeehLbflJbQ0gTDcPXXso5JubkvI3XA197dNqlJC9oxGoOHVWnZdFSPJQ5Ov1r2ADMWMbty3V1GB-jNyK473_sBKGTK-0bG-9FAY1ui9PDAjYpyrk5MCxgPaH2nvQqdPaYds5WNIqr_W1ey6GlwrhZjpd3ytIFwBDyhzWuP2IdVZXEHWhvCq2e3QXvkQeqYzrt4oUJGsugetm77vePrJ1Cc9BgxWXE709bWvYanD3lE%3D)
---
Peter,
In 2023, our team conducted our first domestic rescue in California.
**A 12-year-old girl.** _Trafficked. Drugged. Raped. Held for 45 days in a homeless encampment under a bridge._
_**Our operators physically extracted her.** _
What it takes to be that team is what most people never see. The training. The intelligence work. The willingness to walk into a homeless encampment under a bridge knowing exactly what you might find and what you might have to do to bring a child out alive. The capacity to stay steady when the place you are going to is the worst place a 12-year-old has ever been.
**And underneath all of it, faith.** Our operators are vetted under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure before they ever set foot on a mission – because the work breaks anyone who walks into it without something stronger than their own will to fall back on. **We are the hands and feet of Jesus Christ in the field, and we have been since the day this organization started.** That is not a slogan. It is the load-bearing piece of how a team walks under that bridge and walks back out with a 12-year-old girl alive.
Thanks to God and the work of our operators, she made it home. Her family will never be the same. Neither will our team.
She was one of nine children we recovered in California that year. Each one is a blessing, but know this – _the next child is already missing._
**This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Force Recon scout sniper with two decades of service and 15 overseas deployments. Today, I write to you as the Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity.**
---
[ ](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=051ea43747454832a3e457f7a35a64bf&_e=gIaj_jiIbQc3Uty1ysOAfmVoGxTLIiWcQmf3ypBIr2BzY2uWrk5whzwUs1xOHbqqbtm4NVW7giGcvqYinXdb-MnteMRUwarVYjGu5kGu7aWizF5a97N9rufyxBLrPzV8BNCSclsYnhZEEmIj-R-uo0Ur3NOma9VA-n22yhe7moaOpHyVyf4o8XjbQ9MsVUdE9wClwVhDc9ZNWivRcUkN589Y9a4dg_NB0Tjkd5kH8Dkch_rJCZ1mHby5RipkBQifwA93jbUDeOYvh_HtHlZCS6FZ5FyCHSbpnJO9zLezTTxKf6K47WnAJbIH-1XuqVes23PV_umxWL-vYfBruAGK4W5PFIgVfuMpHMz0ms5BqkLyy1LBmI-_ji22InX1I5w6bszovNpvwbRIe9EC4yUcg_SF-y9RzZka5JcSYZY4Tt83R_BB2s06ynHrK9mMgwcLZRl9rhm4FnOVRrOPrifkhJeEqdetZvjRb2tphUNv-kd4PFOqsKqFHLucBN_oiAF4Pv1ZiSv6_2d1Iv-xjMcCYwmYDaZaBMZJ80tUL5U5HhA91XwmynN7Dz6BRT7NlnGr6dCAHBMJ9t2zDKOtq060LG3bIar5DdBfUGz6vt5j8c9BuUFK_RUFE4mKMoK2PD5G8SLWTBolkL2FtwqGphk_fJezpFlej_evKWvWqeT2eVfHzQaFj7_aa5aZwZPxDoYwgnNoXRZKhACUNfUViAGnV-KkZNqCimnqSSUyKPF1CExXXHVf0MWkm_rtFZZjYN9W2DEZIBCvy9_7MjMygSKgc6x0e2D1kSPkAK3AY47k0yE%3D)
---
**We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Fast forward, and today we are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit network of veteran special operators, first responders, and medical professionals doing the work most organizations cannot.**
In the last 90 days alone, our team has operated across three continents – efforts which entailed:
**✅ Eight American families extracted **from Mexico in February.

**✅ 33 American families and 155 additional Americans** assisted across Israel, Egypt, and Jordan in March.

**✅ 100,000+ meals distributed to individuals in desperate need in Haiti**.

**✅ Three more young teenage children rescued from trafficking situations** in Virginia and West Texas this January.
The work goes back further. **64 evacuated from Ukraine** during active combat in 2022. **58 Christians rescued from persecution** across Asia-Pacific and granted asylum.
For five years we have done all of this from temporary facilities, borrowed space, and on-the-fly logistics. We made it work because we had to. But the demand keeps accelerating, and we cannot train operators fast enough this way.
**So we've just launched an intensive, nationwide capital campaign for the Heroes for Humanity National Training Center – a permanent home for the mission, right here in our home state of Texas.**
**The Training Center is a permanent facility built around the three pillars of our mission – precision personnel rescues, humanitarian and medical aid, and evangelism.** Standardized certification for every operator we put in the field. Medical and trauma training for austere and hostile environments. An OSINT and intelligence hub for ongoing mission planning. And the capacity to train the next generation of operators – at scale, under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure – for as long as the mission lasts.
**Total goal:** $1,000,000 by October.
**First milestone:** $100,000.
[ **Your generous commitment, right now, with a donation of any amount would be incredibly helpful. The strength of this launch will set the tone for our push towards October, and anything you can afford, even if it’s just $25, would be a true blessing.** ](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=051ea43747454832a3e457f7a35a64bf&_e=gIaj_jiIbQc3Uty1ysOAfmVoGxTLIiWcQmf3ypBIr2BzY2uWrk5whzwUs1xOHbqqbtm4NVW7giGcvqYinXdb-MnteMRUwarVYjGu5kGu7aWizF5a97N9rufyxBLrPzV8BNCSclsYnhZEEmIj-R-uo0Ur3NOma9VA-n22yhe7moaOpHyVyf4o8XjbQ9MsVUdE9wClwVhDc9ZNWivRcUkN589Y9a4dg_NB0Tjkd5kH8Dkch_rJCZ1mHby5RipkBQifwA93jbUDeOYvh_HtHlZCS6FZ5FyCHSbpnJO9zLezTTyg6gtQWrMRggMP18Vlu-_pmN2TFT28Y9cl9wsMcOQGp0vmPVFvpqiBLMh2x9Y0vkmTqukv9RkZnh_obriP7V6Bic5MJF16VMiqRkubrY2-rW4aglsdztyLIi9yMndMLUPtvLH6CFpr6gqsfxscAjk7kypb9HfSjS75T5Ua2oijZWIdcaKC2xTyxiFEHQEyb9dZA0SdIdSNgYK4eTBaE02klSxvTGSQwtdsS0H8KXG-FaxpMoREUo-huLtRUtd6T0DpLQvfJNXshu_FPkLTjyNVika1RSPDleT-F2Jyd-xnkcPKX-pX6EK6KwqlNCEyiH0BiBdhLzhIjMVspyRjwJXSHZ7IbFxlcaj22JWjQanaqWObuHw5oZdFtlLs_TCRfom3PViaRXCvu6el2gR3jBWwXPhrq_Y_I9z2ntwyj6DGBEhHsy9RvYFDNz8SI-5OliPgvuidzerQggHS75rjh8SJDZ2Fqzx1VSR4zt8B8zHzUVLC6Bc8w5NhagOR23PFD5Y%3D)

| [MAKE A GIFT TODAY](http://links.stoppingsocialistdems.com/u/click?_t=4dcc2aab65fd4d0da6a107b0eef86d43&_m=051ea43747454832a3e457f7a35a64bf&_e=gIaj_jiIbQc3Uty1ysOAfmVoGxTLIiWcQmf3ypBIr2BzY2uWrk5whzwUs1xOHbqqbtm4NVW7giGcvqYinXdb-MnteMRUwarVYjGu5kGu7aWizF5a97N9rufyxBLrPzV8BNCSclsYnhZEEmIj-R-uo0Ur3NOma9VA-n22yhe7moaOpHyVyf4o8XjbQ9MsVUdE9wClwVhDc9ZNWivRcUkN589Y9a4dg_NB0Tjkd5kH8Dkch_rJCZ1mHby5RipkBQifwA93jbUDeOYvh_HtHlZCS6FZ5FyCHSbpnJO9zLezTTzc3RH1_pbRWvBwtTVC2Xjo8ME_L4pkqXG58LVfNFduGkFW76tSRHTsI_Dd2rXs3NVLAfrlZXfGjZIYQwp-8iK9mP00mTRaXVh4sdJtPPcNg8CzHO3Exa4WtRH6ud2Fr_hyi6-A8W8Heb-ucqOkKewi34wZ0yAhz3Gk0bb3LV2U83X_ctQcC6pwINiMCzZIk5PMzHS3E7H94A2w-skXAQqQ-Uwd7naxLyygRz4aHykxHjW2AkRZ-OXYXvvCXGwirmf51eO31YRd38YiD6zpv3HKbd2YYz7Y_1iHPOmZV5bssR4QprjzNminVve5jVesN10zlU2J1sRbnHt6B33trVSUiUpBolfKYcqHmJPhcDuvjtAbMDDYqXcjbfZ_4whkg6H1qsILeQPHkBd3jxZXYe69-Cocd4H5lChj7s01fuOJbK41dNM15_9wok8Zci7f3-RrFdZr1K_hSu-5VJrQwxI8ScxbqPk9JudFrq9KX9RHlRSGK-5EuBsH2Xoocg7AnSg%3D "MAKE A GIFT TODAY")
---
**As we approach Memorial Day, I would be remiss to not highlight a central piece of the facility, our Foundational Wall** – our way of honoring those who've served, and other heroes among us who deserve our gratitude. **For gifts of $1,000 or more, you can dedicate a brick in honor of someone you choose.** For service members, information will include name, unit, branch, birth and end dates. For non-service members, information may include personal details and attributes, “in loving memory of,” and birth and end dates.
**While that 12-year-old girl in California is now safe, countless other missing children are already out there.** Please, help us build the place that prepares our operators to go find, and bring them home.
Thank you, and let's never forget our mission – _to free the oppressed, so others may live._
Respectfully submitted,
Dennis Price
Founder & CEO
Heroes for Humanity

Hi, it’s Tish James, and I
want you to hear this directly from me:

I’m officially running for reelection as New York’s Attorney General.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260526-partner_ms_tish_em_demandjustice.ixkLVQ&refcode=em20260526-61485&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=61485%2E1407376%2Eq2wEAK ]Before I share more, will you become a Founding Donor of my reelection
campaign by splitting a donation between Demand Justice PAC and my
campaign today?

Since 2019, I’ve had the honor of serving the people of New York. I’ve
taken on the powerful — from big corporations, to the ultra-wealthy, to
powerful politicians like Donald Trump — and delivered real results for
New Yorkers.

When the Trump administration pushed their dangerous and immoral policies
that target our immigrant neighbors, I fought back because protecting all
New Yorkers makes us stronger.

When Donald Trump defrauded the people of New York, I took him to court
and held him accountable.

And as Trump and extreme Republicans ramp up their attacks on everything
we stand for – threatening immigrants’ rights, raising prices for working
people, and launching efforts to roll back voting rights – I’m using the
full power of the attorney general’s office to fight back.

That’s why it’s no surprise Donald Trump is targeting me. He knows I won’t
stop holding him and his administration accountable, and he’s mobilizing
the entire weight of the Department of Justice to come after me because of
it.

But if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it's that you can never back down
from a bully.

I’m running for reelection, and I need you on my side to keep
fighting for the rights of New Yorkers and people all across this country.

Hello Friends,
We are just days away from the June 2nd election, and I want to encourage everyone to make a plan to vote. If you need information on where to vote, how to return your ballot, or where to find a drop box, please visit the California Secretary of State website: Here [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections]
I’m running for Governor because California is becoming too expensive for too many people. Families are struggling with housing costs, groceries, gas prices, and the growing homelessness crisis. We need leadership that understands these challenges and has experience delivering results.
My priorities are straightforward: build more affordable housing, provide relief for working families, support small businesses, expand access to childcare and education, and create more good-paying jobs. _**By David Shuster**_
In an era when American democracy has been corrupted by billionaires, lobbyists, and corporate "dark money," the State of Hawaii has just done something extraordinary. Hawaii's legislature and Governor have attempted to restore a simple and almost quaint principle: corporations and the plutocrat class should not possess the unrestricted right to purchase U.S. election outcomes and buy local, state, and federal governments.
For sixteen years now, our nation has labored beneath the grotesque farce known as "Citizens United," that infamous 5-4 Supreme Court ruling in which the conservative Justices declared that corporations enjoy the same political speech rights of actual citizens.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3db1f7ef-ace4-404e-899e-ed898020be84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The decision was hailed in conservative and GOP circles as a triumph of liberty, similar to how a pick pocket celebrates crowded streets.
Citizens United remains one of the most preposterous acts of judicial alchemy in American history. The Court took a legal fiction--a corporation, that contraption devised primarily to shield wealthy people from accountability--and transformed it into a kind of secular archangel entitled to dump limitless money into elections. The conservative Justices might as well have granted voting rights to parking meters and emotional understanding to slot machines.
The defenders of Citizens United have spent years insisting that money is speech. By that reasoning, a bank vault is a Shakespearean monologue.
The practical consequences have been grotesque. Ever since the 2010 court ruling, our democracy has been lowered into a meat grinder.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3db1f7ef-ace4-404e-899e-ed898020be84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Elections have been dominated by billionaires, industrial syndicates, crypto-speculating degenerates, pharmaceutical monopolists, fossil-fuel emperors, and assorted corporate swamp-creatures whose patriotic devotion to the common good extends as far as the quarterly earnings report.
The average citizen enters this carnival with a vote. The oligarch arrives with a checkbook large enough to purchase senators, governors, think tanks, newspaper columnists, and a Labrador retriever, I mean Fox Business News pundit, trained to bark "free market principles" whenever taxes on hedge funds are mentioned.
And still, our nation has been instructed by most republicans and conservatives to regard this eruption of sewage as democracy.
* * *
###### sponsored
#### **Speaking of corporate money rotting democracy ...**
Citizens United didn't just let billionaires buy politicians. It let them buy the news you read about those politicians.
Every story you scroll past has an owner. A board. A donor. A slant. And most outlets won't tell you whose hand is up the puppet's back.

#### **Hawaii took back their elections. Take back your news feed.**
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3db1f7ef-ace4-404e-899e-ed898020be84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The genius of Hawaii's new law lies in its refusal to bow down before this lunacy. Hawaii has calmly revived an elementary truth: Corporations exist because the public permits them to exist. They are chartered by states. They are granted privileges by states. They are creatures of law--not celestial beings floating above our nation dispensing wisdom from mahogany boardrooms.
Yet under Citizens United, corporations acquired political influence vastly exceeding the influence of ordinary Americans. The nurse in Cleveland possesses one vote. ExxonMobil possesses an ocean of cash sufficient to flood any campaign with political ads, buy all the politicians running for any office, and get nearly total deregulation of the fossil fuel industry.
Hawaii's lawmakers looked at his absurdity and did something almost extinct in modern American politics: they displayed courage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3db1f7ef-ace4-404e-899e-ed898020be84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Not performative courage of the sort practiced by cable-news pundits and congressional windbags who "fight" corruption by sending fundraising emails about it. Actual courage. The sort involving risk. The sort involving powerful enemies. The sort involving corporate lawyers descending upon the state like locusts carrying briefcases.
Naturally, the priesthood of plutocracy is already shrieking. Conservative blowhards who regard billionaires with the reverence medieval monks reserved for saints are clutching their pearls over the possibility that corporations may someday lose the sacred right to purchase attack ads in every television commercial break through the election.
One can barely contain the tears.
These conservatives speak of Citizens United as though it were the Magna Carta rather than a judicial hallucination authored during America's great age of corporate worship. They treat criticism of unlimited campaign spending as an assault on liberty itself. By this logic, a thief's freedom to point a gun at a convenience store clerk and empty the cash register must also be protected as expressions of personal creativity.
But Hawaii has exposed the central fraud.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3db1f7ef-ace4-404e-899e-ed898020be84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Citizens United was never principally about liberty. It was about power. Specifically, the power of concentrated wealth to dominate the political machinery while wrapping itself in claims of constitutional principle.
And let's be clear. This domination has poisoned every aspect of American public life. Congress behaves not like a legislature but as a concierge service for wealthy donors and their corporate Political Action Committees. Climate policy is drafted under the watchful gaze of oil executives. Drug pricing legislation emerges from negotiations conducted with pharmaceutical barons whose business model depends upon charging dying people extravagant sums for crucial medicine. Defense contractors roam through Washington, D.C. and the Pentagon with the logic and stench of slobbering, rabid dogs.
The result is a nation where citizens increasingly suspect--correctly--that the government no longer belongs to them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3db1f7ef-ace4-404e-899e-ed898020be84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That is why Hawaii's law matters far beyond the islands themselves. It represents a rare and glorious refusal to surrender to inevitability. It announces that democracy does not need to remain a subsidiary of multinational capital. If a corporation wants to operate in Hawaii, that corporation must operate in accordance with Hawaii's laws (including the new one) and stop buying local, state and federal election campaigns in Hawaii.
Other states should follow Hawaii's lead immediately.
Let California do it. Let Illinois do it. Let Massachusetts, Oregon, Minnesota, and every state not yet entirely converted into a corporate pass through adopt similar laws. Imagine a coalition of states demanding that democracy belong to citizens again. Imagine governors and lawmakers refusing to accept that American elections must forever function as investment opportunities for corporate interests.
That movement would not merely challenge Citizens United. It would challenge the deeper assumption that wealth should determine political voice.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3db1f7ef-ace4-404e-899e-ed898020be84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Opponents are already howling that this action by the Hawaii legislature and Governor threatens the First Amendment. But the First Amendment was written to protect human liberty and democratic debate--not to guarantee ExxonMobil, pharmaceutical conglomerates, or hedge funds the unlimited ability to purchase political outcomes.
Corporations are not citizens. They do not vote. They do not serve on juries. They do not die in wars. They do not possess consciences, families, or civic obligations. They are legal instruments designed to conduct commerce. Allowing them to dominate elections distorts democracy into something the Founders would not recognize.
Hawaii's legislature and Governor deserve praise not because their law is politically safe, but because it is politically courageous. They recognized that democracy cannot survive indefinitely when money becomes indistinguishable from power. Citizens United remains one of the most preposterous acts of judicial alchemy in American history. The Court took a legal fiction--a corporation, that contraption devised primarily to shield wealthy people from accountability--and transformed it into a kind of secular archangel entitled to dump limitless money into elections. The conservative Justices might as well have granted voting rights to parking meters and emotional understanding to slot machines. The defenders of Citizens United have spent years insisting that money is speech. By that reasoning, a bank vault is a Shakespearean monologue. The practical consequences have been grotesque. Ever since the 2010 court ruling, our democracy has been lowered into a meat grinder. | | ---|---|--- Elections have been dominated by billionaires, industrial syndicates, crypto-speculating degenerates, pharmaceutical monopolists, fossil-fuel emperors, and assorted corporate swamp-creatures whose patriotic devotion to the common good extends as far as the quarterly earnings report. The average citizen enters this carnival with a vote. The oligarch arrives with a checkbook large enough to purchase senators, governors, think tanks, newspaper columnists, and a Labrador retriever, I mean Fox Business News pundit, trained to bark "free market principles" whenever taxes on hedge funds are mentioned. Friend, **Let me take a minute to tell you who I am.**

My name is Tom Cotton. I grew up on my family's cattle farm in Dardanelle, Arkansas.
My folks have farmed this land for seven generations. My dad worked for the state.
My mom was a school teacher and later a principal.

[](http://links.contact.tomcotton.com/u/click?_t=5c7e379ccd6b459ba3c20de95bf89a24&_m=af5b92ea980444179a6b3251214c6077&_e=RG-KC4Lrvd8HNLeKAaWEo0euLYD4OZ9cVI-SCkRsmOYpbbdfo_WINApdPqPyXuOYZF3_JJI2EJ9qTn-D4MhwGKHb1B4MO8A8N_nthXsBYwtXP3xUF6SdvnonlQjQ1sgWnPr8xuPOm1JO_MOtbvH1bIeR_p-V3G-Kk3dSDnf7rcSXiRdlfyIcQYO8giZXdO5Jgedz23Vx-aDh-9lAcyvI4m4_LMYy3TyxRCnjY7wBL1Dm8o3fCI7CJOgj6YJqmZPIilROstRhgvO_sDqYSWE6mzWMMB0dBVh2-UxRwbjF37pKnGttYjd6-TeT5vviAPJ7TW3oREoOXCUyDmUmSQV_1aQ4HBHkXkB21O64sWtRo53W0AQDHiZDkqwjkMJNwK97wH2lfG6UADD_b4iBFGimm0Tql-j9qiDL2IQfe0SpXSmE_NvDoDJohTvoloORLQLiMaksDz0D_Fg9a_T0_d-i3S9--z9Dx0wDc-6FycencDUI1S0F_ZSQ8GlxDDPDfygC)
I worked hard in school. I was on track to be a lawyer.

_Then came September 11._

In the span of a day, _our country was under attack._

**I made a promise to myself that day. I would not spend my life behind a desk. I was going to serve. I was going to fight for America.**

I walked away from the law to enlist in the United States Army.

The brass told me I could be a JAG lawyer.

**I said no.** I wanted to lead men on the front lines. So I became an infantry officer.

[](http://links.contact.tomcotton.com/u/click?_t=5c7e379ccd6b459ba3c20de95bf89a24&_m=af5b92ea980444179a6b3251214c6077&_e=RG-KC4Lrvd8HNLeKAaWEo0euLYD4OZ9cVI-SCkRsmOYpbbdfo_WINApdPqPyXuOYZF3_JJI2EJ9qTn-D4MhwGKHb1B4MO8A8N_nthXsBYwtXP3xUF6SdvnonlQjQ1sgWnPr8xuPOm1JO_MOtbvH1bIeR_p-V3G-Kk3dSDnf7rcQu5Snky3LuahnDMZTmnbbk49qHcjuVE14CfvTMZmOHcDjUQ9nJMsMqAMlmJq7gm7-k7xaOYEUv7EAIM9BL1NgZ9_05_FvP126oEg55TuuJ6oPWidFVDj3pn3YYgW7s3WNLJgCSkOMUZb_LexUOd2fnCiOuDhMi0XflSRvLnCR8nK8fvjahdZsqWb8SpeWOlK_DlHMN77rNcopcenFVLn2npUHEFhejJP-vTZCWgj2YdnMxJHXjNm9UOXX9m_AcWOorUlRpwiodh1bmoTWItBZ_DsJDZFbH56GcB0QcCK5V3CXjjOnCed8JKWABJSwwSXQxNoeCisuafkghOcnc6fkR)
I led a platoon in the streets of Baghdad. I served with the Old Guard at Arlington National Cemetery, laying our heroes to rest. Then I deployed again to Afghanistan.

I came home with a Bronze Star and a Combat Infantryman Badge. But more than that, I came home with a clear mission.

The fight for our country didn't end overseas. It came home with me.

**That's why I ran for Congress. That's why Arkansas sent me to the Senate. And friend, I have not stopped fighting for you and this great country since.**

[](http://links.contact.tomcotton.com/u/click?_t=5c7e379ccd6b459ba3c20de95bf89a24&_m=af5b92ea980444179a6b3251214c6077&_e=RG-KC4Lrvd8HNLeKAaWEo0euLYD4OZ9cVI-SCkRsmOYpbbdfo_WINApdPqPyXuOYZF3_JJI2EJ9qTn-D4MhwGKHb1B4MO8A8N_nthXsBYwtXP3xUF6SdvnonlQjQ1sgWnPr8xuPOm1JO_MOtbvH1bIeR_p-V3G-Kk3dSDnf7rcQaqab2tLhP_8GuO_-I72qzFzaQqZkzdxyIBvp6vbXR5aAOMq8MvofNfchtzNuwYllzOi54GEsWJ6mFHqHjYYEi7GVQcUgJbgIc34mRYbPvkA6FQ6QRoGJm_LRx8f1S-ARgWpoRKFZDZT4YIk2RLpQ0hWDT-cQo68GTkLVvYlwuYGlVpl5vm30ePz5thOIySqnrUY46wHce0beW5yDuxuPqW2YnClBK_QFbDrZUyVbNot9j3H-uV177SgKlJJgTz_N8ujTGHMv-qBn6Q4TApNTt_-v0XJbf9hCcYSdqhDfN0boCj8W50ipiGi1Vop2__-PXS5e7rLU8fgFly9JHVjB2)
I have fought to secure our border. I have fought for our troops and our veterans. I have fought to stand up to Communist China. I have fought for the unborn. I have fought to remove DEI from our schools. I have fought for low taxes, strong families, and the freedoms we hold dear.

Now I am running for re-election. And the Radical Left has me in their crosshairs. They want me silenced. They want my seat. They will spend millions of dollars in dark money to take it.

**I am not afraid of a fight. I never have been. I will never retreat or surrender. But I cannot win this one alone.**

**Will you stand with me today?** **[Can you chip in $25 — or whatever you can spare — to help me keep fighting for America?](http://links.contact.tomcotton.com/u/click?_t=5c7e379ccd6b459ba3c20de95bf89a24&_m=af5b92ea980444179a6b3251214c6077&_e=RG-KC4Lrvd8HNLeKAaWEo0euLYD4OZ9cVI-SCkRsmOYpbbdfo_WINApdPqPyXuOYZF3_JJI2EJ9qTn-D4MhwGKHb1B4MO8A8N_nthXsBYwtXP3xUF6SdvnonlQjQ1sgWQRR2QM8KWN8zwY2WRZE4aXvs37IgzYJKhzaLCEPNO2SjyN0tSrQ7efXNJ3tVr9z5XxLXuCLLYMHOav2GKeTROJ_HepuCq6BGZF71jn9oWm_5Dvs5qxZn5IVHAUCfuP6ApGnplf53SrfyXxW3iyIFV8J2VVNBE_HFGaZxnAHDzSUhBaFRGk99G3Z2t3_dezZArSbpDACOgUw2PaPI5CXka7GWq3NZYEfFEt7BylumqGKugPABkvSRnedxb2zW_9qVS7mQmPySVmrbFxWVVBFPt0BteYvSm8opmG67Y4nZxht_W04DbGPlHWLVc3PnPDoHZbonku_epTM918JyOqvRrM0Cz-ToPCSu5OZj54kZjV4eYsFD9S4wa0_T2h3XuSK14i_u9HLKFEqOuqDxZi_3FA%3D%3D)**

Senator Tom Cotton | | Tom Cotton is a sixth-generation Arkansan born and raised on his family's cattle farm in Yell County. He graduated from Dardanelle High School before earning a bachelor's degree from Harvard University and a J.D. from Harvard Law School. After clerking on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit and briefly practicing law, the September 11 attacks redirected the course of his life. Cotton joined the United States Army as an Infantry Officer and served nearly five years on active duty. He deployed to Iraq with the 101st Airborne Division and to Afghanistan with a Provincial Reconstruction Team. Between those combat tours, he led a platoon with The Old Guard at Arlington National Cemetery — the unit responsible for military honors funerals. His decorations include the Bronze Star Medal, the Combat Infantry Badge, and the Ranger Tab. After leaving active duty in 2009, Cotton ran for Congress in 2012, winning Arkansas's 4th Congressional District. After his term, he set his sights on the Senate, announcing his candidacy in August 2013 and going on to win a decisive victory in the 2014 general election, flipping the seat from Democratic to Republican. Cotton currently chairs the Senate Intelligence Committee, sits on the Armed Services Committee and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, and since November 2024 has served as Chairman of the Senate Republican Conference — the third-ranking position in Senate Republican leadership. Cotton has established himself as a leading figure within the Republican Party, with a particular focus on national security and conservative policy. Tom and his wife Anna have two sons, Gabriel and Daniel.

| | Last month, Trump's Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) released an updated list of water contaminants recommended for testing to ensure the safety of drinking water. Sounds harmless enough, but if you look closer, this is much more sinister. The list includes abortion medications like misoprostol and methotrexate, as well as oral contraceptives. Translation: the Trump administration wants cities and states to start testing its drinking water for traces of these medications. While the EPA claims these benchmarks are merely to "empower local decision makers," the EPA Administrator himself acknowledged that this move is**laying the groundwork for sweeping state and federal restrictions on reproductive health care.** **This administration's attempt to co-opt environmental policy to wage a shadow war on reproductive rights is an egregious abuse of power.** I'm calling on the EPA to _immediately_ abandon this medically and scientifically bankrupt campaign, withdraw any guidance that targets essential reproductive health care, and return to its _actual_ mission of protecting human health and the environment. Instead of working to actually keep our kids and families safe, the Trump administration is targeting reproductive freedom and unraveling key protections against forever chemicals and other deadly substances. We must listen to science. We can't let these fraudulent campaigns run rampant. We must put a stop to this now. Florida is home to more cigar companies than any other state in the country. Brands like Oliva, Padrón, and Fuente, world-class cigar makers, are headquartered in the Sunshine State. They employ thousands of Floridians. They represent a tradition stretching back over 150 years to the Cuban immigrants who built Ybor City into the "Cigar Capital of the World." Governor DeSantis recently sat down with Cigar Aficionado magazine and made clear he's proud of what Florida's cigar industry has built. He explained how he has been a staunch ally of Florida's cigar industry since day one, building relationships with the men and women who run these companies, pushing back against overreaching federal regulations, and ensuring Florida remains the best state in the country to do business. **That's the Florida blueprint: a governor who takes on the federal bureaucracy, protects industries from Washington overreach, and actually delivers results.** RON PAC exists to take that blueprint nationwide, electing conservative fighters in states across America who will stand up to unelected regulators, defend small businesses, and refuse to let Washington call the shots. But that work costs money. And right now, we need your help. **Every donation of $25 or more is automatically entered to win 1 of 10 signed copies of the June 2026 issue of Cigar Aficionado featuring Governor DeSantis' exclusive interview. 10 winners. One great read. A small thank you for standing with us.**

name: Aaron Ford
subject: I never imagined running for governor was in the cards for a kid like me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
I got to be where I am today because of government programs like food stamps and Medicaid.
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=185%2E127862%2EdPKpsm)
Friends,
Growing up, I never imagined running for governor was in the cards for a kid like me. It didn’t even cross my mind!
My family worked hard. My dad worked at a Safeway, and my mom worked odd jobs, but we still struggled. I distinctly remember a night when all my brother and I had for dinner was a stale Skor bar.
That’s why I keep a Skor bar in my office to this day. Not to eat, but to serve as a reminder of where I come from. I don't ever want to forget.
I got to be where I am today because of government programs like food stamps and Medicaid. They uplifted my family out of tough situations.
**It’s horrible to see these same programs get put on the chopping block by MAGA Republicans.**
Our government shouldn’t be in the business of pleasing mega corporations while working families struggle — but our MAGA Governor, Joe Lombardo, is doing exactly that: He doesn’t care about how Trump’s tariffs negatively impact working people, and he takes massive checks from utility corporations that keep raising rates to squeeze families even harder.
Nevada families deserve better, and that’s why I’m running for governor.
**Our government invested in me when I needed it most.** I went on to earn five degrees, become a public school teacher, and serve as Nevada's Attorney General. That's what happens when we invest in people — and as governor, that's exactly what I intend to do.
**[If you’re with me, chip in $5 today and help us build up our grassroots movement to move Nevada forward:](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260526_1_ak.UIdv5T&amount=5&refcode=em20260526-183&t=2&akid=185%2E127862%2EdPKpsm)**

Thank you,
Aaron

clean_body: I got to be where I am today because of government programs like food stamps and Medicaid. Friends, Growing up, I never imagined running for governor was in the cards for a kid like me. It didn’t even cross my mind! My family worked hard. My dad worked at a Safeway, and my mom worked odd jobs, but we still struggled. I distinctly remember a night when all my brother and I had for dinner was a stale Skor bar. That’s why I keep a Skor bar in my office to this day. Not to eat, but to serve as a reminder of where I come from. I don't ever want to forget. I got to be where I am today because of government programs like food stamps and Medicaid. They uplifted my family out of tough situations. It’s horrible to see these same programs get put on the chopping block by MAGA Republicans. Our government shouldn’t be in the business of pleasing mega corporations while working families struggle — but our MAGA Governor, Joe Lombardo, is doing exactly that: He doesn’t care about how Trump’s tariffs negatively impact working people, and he takes massive checks from utility corporations that keep raising rates to squeeze families even harder. Nevada families deserve better, and that’s why I’m running for governor. Our government invested in me when I needed it most. I went on to earn five degrees, become a public school teacher, and serve as Nevada's Attorney General. That's what happens when we invest in people — and as governor, that's exactly what I intend to do. Thank you, Aaron

Friend, I need allies by my side in Congress who will fight to end genocide, end poverty, and build a democracy that puts our rights and our voices first—rather than billionaire bullies and greedy corporations. **Democratic primary elections are happening right now, which means it’s time to fight for real progressives rather than Democrats who are bought by corporations or right-wing-funded super PACs.** I am proud to endorse **Dr. Adam Hamawy** for Congress in New Jersey’s 12th congressional district and **Saikat Chakrabarti** in California’s 11th congressional district, who are the progressive champions we need. Dr. Hamawy is a former combat surgeon who has served in warzones, and has gone on medical missions to Gaza and the West Bank multiple times in the past few years. While caring for patients under bombardment in Gaza, he was offered the chance to evacuate—but he refused to leave until his entire team was safely evacuated. He’s demanding our government spend our tax dollars on Medicare for All, not genocide. Saikat Chakrabarti co-founded Justice Democrats, which helps elect working-class candidates to Congress rather than corporate Democrats. He helped launch the Green New Deal while serving as Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s Chief of Staff, and pro-Palestine groups have lined up to back his race for Congress. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2f185161-4314-40bc-98df-0bd8b1f1eab9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

PORTLAND, Maine - After a bruising week filled with controversy and growing scrutiny, Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Graham Platner appeared in Portland over Memorial Day weekend for a campaign rally alongside Bernie Sanders and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Troy Jackson.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5b0fe7cf-dd99-44e4-935e-97f4890eaf9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The event, billed as a major show of progressive momentum in Maine, often felt less like a rally for Platner and more like a traveling Bernie Sanders event, with Sanders dominating the crowd's attention, applause, and messaging throughout much of the gathering.
The rally came at a difficult moment for Platner's campaign. In recent days, the Democratic candidate has faced backlash over reports involving alleged inappropriate porta potty behavior, as well as criticism surrounding comments viewed as disrespectful toward a Purple Heart recipient. Those controversies have generated significant online discussion and criticism from political opponents and voters alike.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e5cfbb39-e220-4491-b2b3-312e45d202fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Despite the mounting criticism, Platner did not directly address either controversy during his remarks. Instead, he attempted to pivot toward a broader populist message focused on economic inequality, corporate power, unions, and progressive activism.
"We have built a movement," Platner told supporters. "But that is not a testament to one man. That is a testament to this country, to this state, and to all of you."
Throughout his speech, Platner repeatedly portrayed Maine as a state under economic and political assault from corporations, billionaires, and establishment politicians. He described hearing from seniors worried about rising costs, students burdened by debt, fishermen concerned about tariffs and the economy, and families struggling to afford homes and health care.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c4f9557b-41ac-495a-8a6e-c081c249095c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Platner framed the campaign as a movement "of Maine, by Maine, and for Maine," while also embracing rhetoric closely aligned with Sanders' national progressive movement.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/150398ce-dbee-4bfe-a179-55315ff2ab3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The rhetoric throughout the event reflected the increasingly progressive direction of Maine Democrats aligned with Sanders-style politics. Both Platner and Sanders repeatedly attacked corporations, billionaires, health insurance companies, and wealthy political donors, while advocating for expanded government programs, stronger unions, and greater federal involvement in health care and the economy.
At one point, Platner directly attacked Susan Collins, accusing her and other establishment politicians of serving wealthy elites while ordinary Mainers struggle with inflation, housing costs, and economic uncertainty.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/35a0e4b6-2e4b-4d48-9e78-c6b6a3c9078b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"It is a lie intended to serve the billionaire class," Platner said while criticizing what he described as a system benefiting corporations and the wealthy over working Americans.
Sanders later took the stage to loud applause and delivered many of the same themes that have defined his political career for decades. The Vermont senator spoke at length about wealth inequality, health care costs, union power, and what he described as the struggles facing working-class Americans.
"The very richest people in this country have never had it so good," Sanders said, while arguing that millions of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck and struggling to afford food, rent, health care, and education.
Sanders also praised Platner and Jackson, telling the crowd that electing progressive candidates in Maine could help "transform America."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c977ee63-1ea8-48f4-b56f-4f39cca0967e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Vermont senator framed the rally as part of a broader national political movement, claiming that hundreds of thousands of Americans across the country are rejecting what he described as authoritarianism, corporate greed, and attacks on the working class.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/52b23475-d1ac-4aab-a9e7-0b616c1cc11d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jackson, who is seeking the Democratic nomination for governor, also tied his campaign to the same populist economic message promoted by Sanders and Platner. The longtime labor-backed politician has increasingly aligned himself with the progressive wing of the Democratic Party as he attempts to energize left-wing voters ahead of the 2026 election cycle.
The Portland rally highlighted the growing influence Sanders continues to have within Maine Democratic politics, particularly among younger progressive activists and labor-aligned voters. But it also reinforced how closely Platner has tied his campaign to Sanders' brand of national progressive politics at a time when voters are increasingly focused on affordability, public safety, and quality-of-life concerns closer to home.
While supporters inside the rally cheered calls for a "political revolution," critics argue the event reflected a Democratic Party increasingly focused on ideological messaging rather than practical solutions for inflation, crime, housing shortages, and rising costs across Maine communities.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1234d064-475a-4050-b972-d772b4735121?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For Platner, the rally offered a chance to stand beside one of the country's most recognizable progressive political figures during a turbulent week for his campaign. Yet despite the large crowd and energized atmosphere, the controversies surrounding Platner remained largely unaddressed -- lingering in the background of an event that often appeared centered more around Sanders' movement than Platner's candidacy itself.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9ee54a49-5e40-4644-862e-dceb5aa3e361?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

clean_body: By Jon Fetherston, Maine Wire Reporter. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? By Jon Fetherston, Maine Wire Reporter. May 26 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- PORTLAND, Maine - After a bruising week filled with controversy and growing scrutiny, Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Graham Platner appeared in Portland over Memorial Day weekend for a campaign rally alongside Bernie Sanders and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Troy Jackson. The event, billed as a major show of progressive momentum in Maine, often felt less like a rally for Platner and more like a traveling Bernie Sanders event, with Sanders dominating the crowd's attention, applause, and messaging throughout much of the gathering. The rally came at a difficult moment for Platner's campaign. In recent days, the Democratic candidate has faced backlash over reports involving alleged inappropriate porta potty behavior, as well as criticism surrounding comments viewed as disrespectful toward a Purple Heart recipient. Those controversies have generated significant online discussion and criticism from political opponents and voters alike. | | ---|---|--- Despite the mounting criticism, Platner did not directly address either controversy during his remarks. Instead, he attempted to pivot toward a broader populist message focused on economic inequality, corporate power, unions, and progressive activism. "We have built a movement," Platner told supporters. "But that is not a testament to one man. That is a testament to this country, to this state, and to all of you." Throughout his speech, Platner repeatedly portrayed Maine as a state under economic and political assault from corporations, billionaires, and establishment politicians. He described hearing from seniors worried about rising costs, students burdened by debt, fishermen concerned about tariffs and the economy, and families struggling to afford homes and health care. | | ---|---|--- Platner framed the campaign as a movement "of Maine, by Maine, and for Maine," while also embracing rhetoric closely aligned with Sanders' national progressive movement. | | ---|---|--- The rhetoric throughout the event reflected the increasingly progressive direction of Maine Democrats aligned with Sanders-style politics. Both Platner and Sanders repeatedly attacked corporations, billionaires, health insurance companies, and wealthy political donors, while advocating for expanded government programs, stronger unions, and greater federal involvement in health care and the economy. At one point, Platner directly attacked Susan Collins, accusing her and other establishment politicians of serving wealthy elites while ordinary Mainers struggle with inflation, housing costs, and economic uncertainty. | | ---|---|--- "It is a lie intended to serve the billionaire class," Platner said while criticizing what he described as a system benefiting corporations and the wealthy over working Americans. Sanders later took the stage to loud applause and delivered many of the same themes that have defined his political career for decades. The Vermont senator spoke at length about wealth inequality, health care costs, union power, and what he described as the struggles facing working-class Americans. "The very richest people in this country have never had it so good," Sanders said, while arguing that millions of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck and struggling to afford food, rent, health care, and education. Sanders also praised Platner and Jackson, telling the crowd that electing progressive candidates in Maine could help "transform America." | | ---|---|--- The Vermont senator framed the rally as part of a broader national political movement, claiming that hundreds of thousands of Americans across the country are rejecting what he described as authoritarianism, corporate greed, and attacks on the working class. | | ---|---|--- Jackson, who is seeking the Democratic nomination for governor, also tied his campaign to the same populist economic message promoted by Sanders and Platner. The longtime labor-backed politician has increasingly aligned himself with the progressive wing of the Democratic Party as he attempts to energize left-wing voters ahead of the 2026 election cycle. The Portland rally highlighted the growing influence Sanders continues to have within Maine Democratic politics, particularly among younger progressive activists and labor-aligned voters. But it also reinforced how closely Platner has tied his campaign to Sanders' brand of national progressive politics at a time when voters are increasingly focused on affordability, public safety, and quality-of-life concerns closer to home. While supporters inside the rally cheered calls for a "political revolution," critics argue the event reflected a Democratic Party increasingly focused on ideological messaging rather than practical solutions for inflation, crime, housing shortages, and rising costs across Maine communities. For Platner, the rally offered a chance to stand beside one of the country's most recognizable progressive political figures during a turbulent week for his campaign. Yet despite the large crowd and energized atmosphere, the controversies surrounding Platner remained largely unaddressed -- lingering in the background of an event that often appeared centered more around Sanders' movement than Platner's candidacy itself. | | ---|---|--- You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. body:
Supreme Court justices haven’t appeared before Congress in 15 years. | |
---
Peter, Supreme Court justices were supposed to appear before a Senate committee for the first time in 15 years last week. **Instead, they wormed their way out of testifying and canceled their appearance.** They may not want to show their faces and answer to us. But that isn’t stopping them from asking for taxpayer dollars from the very Americans whose voting rights they just gutted. **The fact of the matter is, it’s Congress’ job to haul the justices before committees and make the justices answer the hard questions the American people have for them.** Why are communities already losing representation because of their rulings? Why does the Court continue operating under a cloud of ethics scandals and billionaire influence? Why do so many Americans feel like powerful institutions answer to everyone except the people? This Supreme Court has done too much harm to act like business as usual. **It’s past time for Congress to demand accountability and exercise as a check and balance over this corrupt, out-of-control Court.** No institution in this country should be above accountability—especially one making decisions that impact millions of people every single day. **Congress can’t let this moment pass without a fight.** **[Congress can’t let the justices wriggle out of answering to the American people. Write to your Senator today and demand they subpoena the Supreme Court justices so they can demand accountability and answers!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxndm3iNHxw8Kwqb1GA0NQgB-EblSE3_95j1JPTyXKkNwJbSG_7-juOI4bmnLunUrQcF8_1J_xYsvy3iJSxutUcLnyhNsfQMGXU2bQEiqq2CxEpNY8wMObNNIjM5FkayxJ1Sei0r0QTby2CP0PcwRPfHmeXDu3ZRo6JyMok9Ow3Glo6OtaJuKAdcS5r5RPhKbIDg-fqRcG0orSCpv0d_UsYmAB9Ov3h-VdXv3Sc5J0Qy0uR75eiAaLYlJCgqqJ2kpWPl0dIADV5f762kNkrJWas4BX0FUKLd1H2i29KcviND16A9hFYz25L2lPBDOuLcKo/4qy/neL4adzoRvmwVc7_CBjzHg/h0/h001.6Lj9veoaCDZlDELAB99PM7a5Y1K9g98-Q_OZCpeHg-4)** [SIGN & SEND](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxndm3iNHxw8Kwqb1GA0NQgB-EblSE3_95j1JPTyXKkNwJbSG_7-juOI4bmnLunUrQcF8_1J_xYsvy3iJSxutUcLnyhNsfQMGXU2bQEiqq2CxEpNY8wMObNNIjM5FkayxJWSCtH2ur21rQbn-SK5kx7V_iKfXsAnmwwSjvBhoSR6Bk6xuN1SU7ZmQjkAYncOsU-Ug-0ADkUDKVLrH4aJqpfN5ctSiqz9SkT1Kxongh8YDDdw4JIa6Z0panzBvmtsU9yHj08GE49LXzsAUru2lVKdiot5RabVJfVPbooCYR6LZfMfxoOyg3AMv_DvVCwDlj/4qy/neL4adzoRvmwVc7_CBjzHg/h1/h001.il-c1tiZAr0yI5bwMkmOFkCAwl-ITkC-q0yBr7G92UA) The Court’s decision gutting voting rights isn’t an isolated incident. It’s just the latest move by a system that’s been captured and manipulated to put wealth and power over the people. **The Supreme Court has been taking power away from ordinary people for years, and working families are paying the price in ways they feel every single day.** People can’t afford groceries, rent, or prescriptions. Workers are fighting for fair wages while corporations spend millions capturing the courts and Congress. The wealthy and powerful have gotten everything they paid for—and our voices are being taken away. **It’s Congress’ job to step in and end the corruption, attacks on democracy, and unconstitutional action. Their constituents are paying attention, and people have woken up to this system that’s been broken on purpose.** We’re demanding a political system that works for us, not the wealthy, corporations, and dark money. The justices are resisting appearing before Congress, hoping their request for funds can just be an email. But it can’t—Congress must require serious answers for the Court’s actions if they want a penny more of taxpayer dollars. The last time Supreme Court justices appeared before the Senate was 15 years ago. Justices Breyer and Scalia faced questions about the myriad scandals that were already facing them back then, including billionaire-funded trips, political appearances, and the lack of a code of ethics. **We need Congress to bring that energy now, and demand answers from the justices face-to-face.** **When enough people demand change loudly enough and long enough, Washington has no choice but to listen. We’re demanding Congress step up, demand accountability from the corrupt Supreme Court, and fight for a political system that works for everyday people again.** **[Send a message to your Senator now. Tell them you’re watching, you expect them to do their job, and demand that they make the Supreme Court justices answer the hard questions.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm396MCpkY7Ue0aOf7CTWHOaxndm3iNHxw8Kwqb1GA0NQgB-EblSE3_95j1JPTyXKkNwJbSG_7-juOI4bmnLunUrQcF8_1J_xYsvy3iJSxutUcLnyhNsfQMGXU2bQEiqq2CxEpNY8wMObNNIjM5FkayxJpXhP5ih-D4fVc4cW8IoRvMxBdDHKqcq8ri7YpAWqmhZFjZ5fQjvt_n_ZiG1ndnhYCO_DULAo83fhGIWd6lWPIte-q9R-jESIP4H7dLSpdF0Ney5xrcNhLpyRQ1PD1wSW_cVoibzu0OOlwqJ-DAhnjdc3p5dSdbempSeoJOYVpFQ-BKgtxpgKikrViU2wz0bS/4qy/neL4adzoRvmwVc7_CBjzHg/h2/h001.gD0wckgmd2uD9MXMSv8sUcqzE2AP7lk6OZ7qF_fciHE)** Thank you for demanding Congress do its job, Ken’Travius Coleman

We’re demanding Congress step up, demand accountability from the corrupt Supreme Court, and fight for a political system that works for everyday people again. Thank you for demanding Congress do its job, Ken’Travius Coleman United for Democracy Paid for by United for Democracy. | | Sent via . clean_body: I’m doubling down on my support. | | | | | ---|--- Earlier this year, I announced that I donated over $400,000 from my campaign account to 23 state parties to ensure Democrats win up and down the ballot in November. I wanted to reach out and share an update: Our team has raised an additional $400,000 to give to state parties in North Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Maine, Georgia, and Alaska. These six states have some of the most competitive Senate races of the cycle – and I think Democrats can win if we have the resources we need to put up a fight. We need to gain four seats to take back the Senate, which means we need to put up a strong defense in Michigan and Georgia, AND a strong offense in Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Alaska. This money is how we fight back – hiring organizers, airing ads, and reaching out to more voters. Because Democrats can’t just talk the talk about the midterm elections being critical. We have to put our money where our mouth is. Republicans certainly are. Billionaire donors and giant corporations are giving them buckets of money they can use to cling onto their power in the midterms. That’s why I’m doubling down on my support for these state parties. This team has now helped contribute over $800,000 now to state parties across the country this cycle. We have an open U.S. Senate seat in Montana, and while this seat has long been considered safely Republican, we cannot afford to take anything for granted in this environment. Our Senate map this cycle is challenging. Republicans are defending far more seats than Democrats, and our resources are stretched across the country. Open seats like this one demand early attention and strong grassroots support. Kurt Alme has spent his career serving the people of Montana as a prosecutor, public servant, and leader committed to the rule of law. He served as U.S. Attorney during both Trump Administrations, focusing on public safety, combating drug trafficking, and protecting Montana communities. Now, he's stepping forward to serve again, but he won't have an easy path. Democrats see this race as a top opportunity. They will spend heavily, organize aggressively, and do everything they can to flip this seat. We've seen this playbook before – flooding states with outside money and misleading attacks in an effort to gain control of the Senate. We can't let that happen here. Kurt just got into this race. He needs the resources to introduce himself to voters, share his record, and communicate a clear conservative vision for Montana's future. This race is about more than one seat. It's about maintaining a Senate Republican majority that can advance a conservative agenda, confirm strong judicial nominees, and provide a check on Washington's excesses. If we lose ground here, we risk losing our ability to lead effectively. Kurt Alme is the kind of candidate we need. He's steady, principled, and focused on results. I hope you'll stand with us. John Thune Republican Leader P.S. Montana is a critical hold for Republicans, and this open seat will be a top target for Democrats. **Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. **Peter, today is Election Day in the Texas primary runoffs.** By tonight, Texas will officially be full speed ahead towards the general election in November.
And here’s the thing, right now, we’re seeing a movement across Texas because people like you decide to show up, vote for better leadership, and help build the kind of campaign that can win.
After today’s decision, we need to work on turning this momentum into voter turnout in November, so we want to know:
If you knew a **$5** donation would help elect Gina as the next Governor of Texas and finally vote Greg Abbott out, _would you chip in?_
If you knew **$5** would help power voter contact and organizing across the big state of Texas, so we can reach people who don’t always get reached, _would you step up?_
If you knew **$5** would help us fight back when Abbott and his billionaire buddies flood the airwaves with attacks, _would you be part of this fight?_
_It’s true, Peter_ — just **$5** will go a long way toward doing all of these things. We know it doesn’t seem like that amount makes a real impact, but every single dollar counts to help elect Gina and power the fight for change happening in Texas right now.
That’s why we set a goal to raise **$100,000 by May 31st** , and we’re counting on grassroots supporters to help us get there.

It promises more tailpipe pollution — more cancer, COPD, asthma, blood clots, strokes, and heart attacks. All while forcing more reliance on costly gas. The EPA’s job is to make our air cleaner. Instead, Trump’s EPA is making us sicker. I KNOW you’re not OK with this Peter. We need your help.These rollbacks are horrible for the environment. They’re horrible for people's health. They drive up everyone’s costs. It’s going to take a major campaign to hold them accountable — so we’re asking: Can you renew your LCV membership for just $15 today? We’re racing to meet a $30,000 goal this month, and every contribution really matters. Here’s the thing: Trump isn’t doing this alone. He’s aided and enabled by congressional Republicans, blocking affordable clean energy and propping up costly fossil fuels every step of the way. But data shows that in many of the battleground House districts, nearly half of voters think lowering the cost of utility bills should be a top priority for Congress. And 54% of swing voters in those districts disapprove of Trump and congressional Republicans blocking affordable, clean, wind and solar energy. The Trump administration’s choices to make us sicker, drive up costs, and force reliance on gas are WILDLY unpopular with everyday people and families all over the country when they hear about it. We need to be reaching these people. And we need your help to do it. Right now, we’re in the middle of a major ad campaign to hold these officials accountable for how their actions are harming the people they were elected to represent and raising their costs. We’re putting our message up in swing districts in Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Arizona right now. This campaign could have a HUGE impact, but only with the help of supporters like you. We need to raise $30,000 this month to amp up our organizing to hold MAGA lawmakers accountable. Renew your LCV membership today to help us amplify our message before November’s midterm elections. Right now, $15 is all it takes >> RENEW YOUR MEMBERSHIP >> Thank you for everything you do for the environment, Peter. Chris Brooks Vice President, Membership League of Conservation Voters This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Hi friend, I’m proud to endorse my colleague, Congresswoman Linda Sanchez, in her re-election campaign for California’s newly redrawn 41st District – and I’m asking you to join me in supporting her ahead of the June 2 primary.
Linda is one of the most effective champions for working families in Congress, and she’s facing an extreme MAGA primary opponent who wants to build Trump’s border wall, supports the voter suppression bill known as the Save America Act, and wants to “protect traditional families” – which we all know is code for rolling back our rights.
California’s new district maps split her current district (CA-38) in two, so she’s running in a competitive primary in a newly drawn district, and she could really use our help in these final days before the election.
Will you split a donation between Linda’s campaign and mine today to help her win the primary and help us get ready to win the House in November? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em-sanchez]
CONTRIBUTE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em-sanchez?amount=50]
Linda is a lifelong Californian and the daughter of Mexican immigrants who came to this country and built a life in Southern California. She grew up working class, put herself through UC Berkeley and UCLA Law, and spent years as a labor lawyer fighting for workers’ rights before she ran for office.
And right now, she is one of the loudest, most uncompromising voices in Congress speaking out against the Trump administration’s anti-immigrant agenda and ICE’s terror. She has refused to fund ICE's raids on her community. She has fought for real accountability measures, like body cameras, requirements that agents can't hide their identities behind masks, and more rigorous hiring standards.
She has never forgotten where she came from, never wavered from her values, and she shows up every day to fight for the people of her district.
We need to keep strong Democrats like Linda in Congress to fight back against this lawless administration, and with the primary in less than two weeks, she needs our help. I want to do everything I can to make sure she wins in June and again in November, so will you split a donation between our campaigns right now? Derek, this
November, we have a choice here in Pennsylvania.

We have a choice between politicians who take their cues from Donald Trump
or leaders who answer to the good people of Pennsylvania.

We have a choice between extremists who put their party loyalty first, or
leaders who believe every Pennsylvanian should have the freedom to worship
how they choose, vote in free and fair elections, build a good life, and
be treated with dignity and respect no matter what they look like, where
they come from, or who they love.

We have a clear choice between the chaos, cruelty, and corruption of the
far-right — or a different path forward.

We can push back. We can say enough is enough. We can reclaim our power
and stand together in common purpose.

That’s the Pennsylvania way.

And if we’re going to keep moving Pennsylvania forward, we can’t afford to

No one is coming to do this work for us, so it’s on each and every one of

Peter,

_**Next year, our nation turns 250 years old.**_

Two and a half centuries ago, 56 patriots pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor to build the freest, greatest country the world has ever known. They didn't do it so politicians like Tim Walz and Peggy Flanagan could hand it over to lawbreakers and fraudsters.

But that's exactly what's happening in Minnesota right now.

While families like yours work hard, pay your taxes, and play by the rules, Democrat leaders in St. Paul are. They're rolling out the red carpet for illegal migrants — many of whom have criminal records — and tying the hands of the brave officers trying to keep our communities safe.

And it gets worse.

_**Just weeks ago, federal agents raided 22 sites across the Twin Cities investigating hundreds of millions of dollars in fraud through Medicaid and childcare programs. Hard-earned taxpayer money — your money — stolen right out from under us while Walz and Flanagan looked the other way. **_****

I didn't spend 21 years as a Marine infantryman and Navy SEAL officer — deploying nine times to over 70 countries — to come home and watch this happen to the country I love.

My name is Adam Schwarze. On my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after 9/11, I enlisted in the Marine Corps. I later became a Navy SEAL, and I've been shot at, had bombs dropped on me, and faced enemies in hand-to-hand combat. _

_But I'll tell you something honestly: **watching Democrats let criminals steal billions from American taxpayers while shielding illegal migrants from federal law enforcement may be one of the most egregious betrayals I've ever witnessed.**

If we don't stop Walz, Flanagan, and their radical allies here in Minnesota, they'll take this same playbook nationwide:

* Sanctuary cities protecting criminal illegal aliens
* Billions in taxpayer fraud with no accountability

clean_body: As we approach America's 250th birthday, radical Democrats in Minnesota are protecting illegal migrants while billions in taxpayer dollars vanish into fraud. I refuse to stay silent. | Peter, Next year, our nation turns 250 years old. Two and a half centuries ago, 56 patriots pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor to build the freest, greatest country the world has ever known. They didn't do it so politicians like Tim Walz and Peggy Flanagan could hand it over to lawbreakers and fraudsters. But that's exactly what's happening in Minnesota right now. While families like yours work hard, pay your taxes, and play by the rules, Democrat leaders in St. Paul are. They're rolling out the red carpet for illegal migrants — many of whom have criminal records — and tying the hands of the brave officers trying to keep our communities safe. And it gets worse. Just weeks ago, federal agents raided 22 sites across the Twin Cities investigating hundreds of millions of dollars in fraud through Medicaid and childcare programs. Hard-earned taxpayer money — your money — stolen right out from under us while Walz and Flanagan looked the other way. ** I didn't spend 21 years as a Marine infantryman and Navy SEAL officer — deploying nine times to over 70 countries — to come home and watch this happen to the country I love. My name is Adam Schwarze. On my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after 9/11, I enlisted in the Marine Corps. I later became a Navy SEAL, and I've been shot at, had bombs dropped on me, and faced enemies in hand-to-hand combat. But I'll tell you something honestly: watching Democrats let criminals steal billions from American taxpayers while shielding illegal migrants from federal law enforcement may be one of the most egregious betrayals I've ever witnessed. name: Mallory McMorrow
subject: Washington is rolling back civil rights. Michigan is not sitting back.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McMorrow for Michigan
body:
# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4799%2E898137%2E0kx__0)
Hi there,
I wanted to reach out because something pretty huge happened recently, and I wanted to make sure you heard about it.
If you haven’t been watching the news, last month the US Supreme Court handed down a devastating ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_. They basically gutted Section 2 of the 1965 Voting Rights Act. If you remember your history, that landmark law was put in place to stop states from diluting the votes of minorities — especially Black voters who had been systematically disenfranchised for generations.
Section 2 was our shield against that kind of discrimination. But now? The Supreme Court basically said that as long as politicians claim they’re just playing "party politics," dismantling people’s voting power is totally fine. It’s infuriating, and as Justice Elena Kagan wrote in her dissent, it renders this crucial federal law "all but a dead letter."
Washington is actively rolling back civil rights. But I promise you, **we are not sitting back in Michigan.**
**We’ve become the first state in the entire country since that awful ruling to hold a legislative hearing on state-level protections to enshrine those exact voting rights. I’m incredibly proud to have co-sponsored these bills and voted them right out of the Elections Committee to build a state-level shield.**
**Our bills will restore those anti-discrimination protections on the state level, expand language access for voters, and force real local transparency. Because at the end of the day, democracy only works if _everyone_ has an equal say.**
**The Constitution is clear: states run elections. When federal protections falter, it is up to us to lead the way and show the rest of the country how it's done.**
